articleTitle: A Comprehensive Survey on Infant Biometric Recognition
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: Using biometric technologies to identify and track infants based on their distinct physiological traits is known as infant biometrics. Infants are particularly difficult to identify and authenticate because of their quick physical development, lack of cooperative behaviour, and extreme sensitivity to invasive operations. This study investigates novel techniques for recording and evaluating biometric characteristics unique to infants, including fingerprints, palmprints, ear shapes, and face features. ECG is a widely used tool for identifying cardiac disorders since it detects the electrical activity of the heart. As a biometric, ECG can offer an intrinsic, one-of-a-kind identification as every person's heart waveform is different. From this study we come to know that just like a adult biometric can be done through ECG in the same way an infant biometric through ECG will be feasible and accurate. Although recording and interpreting ECG data from babies presents certain difficulties but advances in signal processing and technology can make this method more and more practical.

articleTitle: Automating Legal Expertise: A Rule-Based Approach to Legal Reasoning Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: This research explores the development of an expert system for legal decision-making, specifically designed for the Indian legal context, utilizing Prolog for case-based reasoning. The Indian legal system, governed by the Indian Penal Code (IPC), various constitutional laws, and legal precedents, relies heavily on judicial decisions to inform future rulings. Prolog, a logic programming language with rule-based inference capabilities, presents an effective solution for automating such legal reasoning. In this paper, we construct an expert system that processes legal facts, applies relevant sections of Indian laws, and matches current legal cases to relevant prior judgments to deliver case-based legal decisions. The system incorporates key provisions from the IPC, such as sections dealing with theft, criminal offenses, and contract disputes, using legal precedents from landmark Indian cases to demonstrate its applicability. This research highlights the system’s effectiveness in handling rule-based legal reasoning while discussing the challenges posed by ambiguous legal language, scalability, and real-world complexities. We conclude by proposing enhancements, such as integrating machine learning techniques to refine case interpretation and automate more complex aspects of the Indian judicial process.

articleTitle: Machine Learning based Effort Estimation Models for Software Development Projects related Datasets with diverse features
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: This research evaluates the performance of machine learning models for the estimation of software effort using diverse datasets with distinct feature sets and varying training-test splits. To address the risks of under or overestimation in project management, the study employs robust data preprocessing, feature engineering, and selection techniques. Through extensive experimentation, the study analyzes model accuracy using multiple metrics such as Mean Absolute Error, R-squared, precision, recall, F1-score, and Receiver Operating Characteristic Area Under the Curve. Preprocessing techniques, including feature scaling and outlier removal, were applied to reduce overfitting and improve generalization. Performance was assessed using various indicators, with results showing that the stacked ensemble model consistently outperformed other models like Linear Regression, Support Vector Regression, and Gradient Boosting in generating accurate predictions across datasets. The analysis revealed that no single data split yielded optimal performance for all datasets; instead, different datasets performed best under customized splits. Larger datasets performed well with splits like 70-30, while smaller ones exhibited overfitting even after preprocessing. Models like Random Forest, XGBoost, and Gradient Boosting demonstrated robust performance, especially on larger datasets, while smaller datasets highlighted challenges with models like K-Nearest Neighbors and Naive Bayes due to overfitting and poor generalization. These findings underscore the importance of adapting data-splitting strategies to the characteristics of individual datasets, offering a pathway to improve estimation accuracy in diverse software development scenarios. The research highlights that larger datasets enable better generalization, while smaller datasets require careful model and preprocessing choices to mitigate overfitting and achieve reliable results.

articleTitle: Skin Lesion Prediction and Classification using Deep Learning methods
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: In the past decade, The Skin Cancer is observed to be a most common disease. Eventually it is not considered as a fatal disease if properly treated. The early diagnosis is more important for the proper cure. As per the reports, it is said over 20% of the population in Canada, US are mostly affected. It is also reported that, with respect to the age, the chance of getting affected by the skin cancer is more. The better recovery is seen once the early diagnosis is done. As per the available medical records, the recovery rate is huge and the fatal rate is less. In this research, investigations on identifying the suitable methodology in deep learning technique is carried out. The research gave the optimum solution of efficient skin cancer prediction with an accuracy of 99.6%. The EfficientNetB0 methodology with the Adam optimizer is observed with computationally improved in performance and accuracy when compared with the state of the art methods.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Machine Learning Models in Network Intrusion Detection Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: Networks plays a vital role in modern society and cyber security has become a critical area that needs to be acknowledged. A crucial part of cybersecurity frameworks intended to track network traffic and spot suspicious activity, and malicious activity is an intrusion detection system(IDS). Integrating machine learning (ML) algorithms into IDS greatly improves the system’s ability to study complex network traffic and accurately identify abnormal patterns. In addition, the incorporation of algorithms reduces the complexity of large data sets and the training time of models. In this paper, we propose the application of three algorithms Decision Tree(J48), SVM, and Naïve Bayes on the NSL-KDD dataset. These algorithms are applied after preprocessing dataset, which includes feature selection and class imbalance resolution. After applying the aforementioned algorithms, we assessed their performance based on metrics such as confusion matrix, accuracy. The results of the environment clearly indicate which algorithm works best with the data set and achieves high accuracy with minimal time required to build the model.

articleTitle: Classifying the DNA sequence using Optimized Naive Bayes Approach: A Comparative Analysis of Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: In bioinformatics, the exact classification of DNA sequences is essential to increasing comprehension of genetic structures and functionalities. This research introduces an enhanced Naive Bayes approach (ENB) specifically designed to handle more complexities related to DNA sequence data. This research integrates advanced feature weighting and optimized probability estimation techniques to enhance classification accuracy substantially. The proposed work demonstrated superior efficacy to traditional ML algorithms like Random Forest, SVM, Decision-Trees, K-Nearest Neighbors, Gradient Boosting etc. The proposed method attained a level of accuracy of 98%, and proposed approach performs better than the other models, with 94% accuracy in Logistic Regression coming in second.

articleTitle: Revolutionizing Diet and Fitness Tracking with AI: A User-Centric Approach to Nutrition and Wellness
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: The proposed Diet Recall is designed to provide an integrated solution for diet tracking, fitness management, and nutritional analysis through a user-friendly mobile platform. Modern lifestyles often lack consistency in healthy dietary practices, and this application serves as an accessible tool to bridge the gap between health intentions and actual actions. It enables users to monitor their food intake, analyze nutrient content, set and track fitness goals, and receive personalized meal and workout recommendations based on preferences and health conditions. The application follows a user-driven approach, leveraging key personal data such as age, weight, height, activity level, and dietary restrictions to estimate daily maintenance calories using the Harris-Benedict formula. The core recommendation engine employs K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) and content-based filtering to generate tailored diet and exercise plans. Data processing is efficiently handled using Pandas and NumPy, while Firebase powers the backend, and Flutter ensures a cross-platform experience. This work demonstrates the potential of AI-driven digital health solutions in fostering sustainable behavioral changes and long-term wellness.

articleTitle: A Survey on Diabetes Mellitus Using Machine Learning Classifiers
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: Diabetes is a chronic illness problem that arises from insufficient insulin production or insufficient insulin use by the body. Most of causes of death, diabetes is linked to the interplay of lifestyle, psychosocial factors, medical problems, and risk factors that are hereditary and demographic. However, the evaluation measures and datasets used in each article vary when it comes to algorithms. It focuses on creating systems that do not require direct programming by automatically learning from data and gaining ideas to improve their performance. It enables systems to examine data, acquire experience, and make choices, allowing them to adjust and raise their level of performance over time. Health professionals, such as doctors, have benefited to assistance in treating, analysing, and diagnosing medical issues as well as identifying illness. This can assist patients in making an initial diagnosis of diabetes and is used by medical professionals as a resource.

articleTitle: Brain Tumor Detection and Classification Using Deep Learning on MRI Images
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: One's life is very much precious and Brain tumors are a critical concern to the life of a person. If they are not identified on time, they can take life an individual. So, it becomes important to identify them as soon as possible. If identified in time, this can be the point of difference between a life and death of an individual. If found early, we will be able to treat them accordingly. In order to have much clearer pictures of tumors that we will be working on, we will operate with a dataset comprising MRI images of the human brain. The dataset includes both tumor and non-tumor MRI pictures, realizing the wide-ranging review of anomalies that occur in the brain. The model used here is Visual Geometry Group (VGG-16). When the model detects a tumor, then it becomes important to classify it. After testing, the brain tumors are classified into three different types, including glioma, meningioma, and pituitary tumors. Different classes of the tumors are useful for making treatment plans and ensembling the need of each patient.

articleTitle: Pneumonia Detection Based on Image Analysis Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: Pneumonia is an inflammatory disease of the lung led by many parasites, viruses, and, in some instances, pathogens. Pneumonia is a condition that can sometimes be fatal as it is especially serious in immune-compromised people, geriatric patients, and young children. Based on the principles of medical image analysis using various deep learning algorithms, such as ResNet, Inception, and VGG, the diagnosis of the patient below, which has been diagnosed with pneumonia from the patient's x-ray and CT scan images, shall be worked out by the authors, enabling early pneumonia diagnosis for proper and timely treatment of the disease.

articleTitle: Hacking LLMs: A Technical Analysis of Security Vulnerabilities and Defense Mechanisms
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) such as GPT-4 and Google’s Gemini have revolutionized the landscape of artificial intelligence, enabling sophisticated natural language processing capabilities across diverse domains. However, the rapid adoption of these models has unveiled a spectrum of security vulnerabilities exploitable by adversaries [1], [2]. This paper presents a comprehensive analysis of various attack vectors targeting LLMs, including prompt injection, data poisoning, model inversion, and side-channel attacks. We examine real-world incidents and vulnerabilities discovered in widely-used LLMs like ChatGPT and Gemini [3], highlighting the intricate mechanisms through which these attacks compromise model integrity and user trust. Furthermore, we explore existing defense mechanisms and best practices, emphasizing runtime protection systems, adversarial training approaches, and robust access control systems [4], [5]. Building upon these foundations, we introduce a novel Multi-Layer Defense Framework with Dynamic Trust Scoring, designed to enhance the security and robustness of LLM deployments through dynamic evaluation and adaptive response systems. By dissecting recent advancements in LLM security research and proposing innovative defense strategies, this paper aims to guide the development of resilient defenses against the evolving landscape of AI-driven threats.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Techniques For Dental Caries Detection And Prosthodontics: A Systematic Review
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: Deep learning applications are increasing in dental caries detection and prosthodontics. However, the current growth and execution of deep learning in dental applications have not been evaluated and presented thoroughly. One of the major challenges to make the dental application more intelligent is to acquire knowledge and information from complex, multi dimensional and diverse structures. Current research has recorded a positive result in handling complex, heterogeneous, badly documented and mostly unstructured dental records. The classification still holds certain limitations even after the integration of many new novel deep learning modern applications to classify more robust and novel insight from the data for analysis. This structured review explores the burgeoning role of Deep Learning in dental caries classification and prosthodontics, focusing on its application in various aspects such as tooth shade selection, restoration design, and classifying facial changes in patients with removable prostheses.

articleTitle: Identification of Negative Intent in Social Media Posts Using Natural Language Processing
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: Daily content viewing and/or posting on social media is very common and influences people across all geographies using numerous strategies and ways. A number of daily activities over web platforms like YouTube in terms of posting, watching, and commenting on videos. This is a report that contains a quickly expanding number of online channels where users post, jot down, and comment on a wide range of topics. NLP is applied to quickly take information from online or web content, that will facilitate your business in very different and numerous ways. Customer-specific data can be easily extracted using NLP, and this data can then be used to create advertising campaigns that are specifically targeted to your customers. This assists in introducing your company to the appropriate target market, which is more likely to convert. The paper will perform the critical analysis of versatile methodologies adapted by various researchers for negative intent identification in social networking sites. The paper will also try to observe the challenges associated with the same. This paper will also analyze the usage of NLP in identifying the negative intent in social media posts.

articleTitle: The Symphony of Style: An Extensive Examination of Determination Mechanisms in Deep Learning-Inspired Outfit Suggestions
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: In the field of the fashion industry, the introduction of deep learning technology has taken an innovative revolution by providing assistance in the construction of intellectual systems that are intelligent to deliver personalized ensemble recommendations. In this research work, an innovative ensemble recommendation structure called Deep Learning VGG16 (Visual Geometry Group 16) recommender is presented. The proposed method allows a deep learning model VGG16 to understand complex patterns and developments resulting from a vast group of fashion images. In order to increase the user experience and greater participation in the well-established fashion industry, the system offers personalized ensemble ideas. The important, core and fundamental component of the system is VGG16, consisting of 13 convolutional layers and 3 fully connected layers, which is used to support the analysis of fashion images. A cutting-edge convolutional neural network (CNN) model is improved over a large and diverse collection of fashion images. Model will extract advanced high-level information and statistics with the capability to distinguish particulars in colour patterns, clothing combinations, and stylistic elements. Using this process of development, the system becomes better at identifying user preferences and fashion trends.

articleTitle: Leveraging Statistical Analysis Using Virtual Reality in Impulsive Buying: A SEM-based Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: Impulsive Buying Behaviour is a commonly used practice now to attract diverse crowds for shopping. The shoppers are more into buying without planning when they find their favourite products at very affordable prices. The urge to own the products gradually increases for the consumers. This study determines how impulsive buying can greatly influence the buying patterns and buying behaviour of consumers. Low-budget-friendly products at affordable pricing are preferred by consumers. Therefore, companies are more focused on having such strategies which causes impulsive buying. To accomplish this, companies approach influencers to motivate and persuade consumers who are usually GenZ and other fashionable people who believe in buying instantly. Impulsive Buying is mainly concerned with buying instantly without giving much thought to the budget because the products are already very affordable. Brands are more into the strategy to induce more shopping. Impulsive buying doesn't happen on products priced higher than expected. The paper uses Virtual temptations as the driving force to understand how virtual temptations drive impulsive buying on retail-commerce platforms now. Information and Normative social influence play a significant role in impulsive buying, whereas informational social influence is more significantly related to impulsive buying. Platform reputation and social influencers play a significant role in impulsive buying. Companies approach influencers who have good content and share quality content more often. The content of influencers is more convincing, and they share it appropriately. Influencers virtually tempt their followers to buy more products they try and share. The products are recommended, and since they are priced so low, consumers on a click purchase them instantly.

articleTitle: A Content-Based Filtering Approach for Personalized Movie Recommendations
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: The recommendation system of today has made it simple to locate the necessities. Movie recommendation systems are designed to assist movie buffs by making recommendations for films to see, saving them the trouble and effort of having to sort through hundreds or even millions of options. The Recommender System has become a major area of research because it helps people find things online by making suggestions that are similar to what they are looking for. In this paper, we introduce a system called MOVIEHOPE for recommending movies. It uses a content-based filtering method that uses the user’s preferences and the item’s description to make a profile. In CBF, we use keywords to describe items instead of the user’s profile to show what they like or do not like. In plain English, the CBF algorithm likes or recommends things that were liked in the past. It looks at how items have been rated before and suggests the best item that fits.

articleTitle: Revolutionizing Customer Experience Through NLP and Sentiment Analysis Strategies
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: The objective of this paper is to highlight Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) neural network’s role in improving Customer Experience (CX). Sentiment Analysis (SA) and Natural Language Processing (NLP) are used as primary methodology for interpreting real-time customer feedback and preferences. BiLSTM models can comprehend contextual understanding at a high level because it analyzes text bidirectionally. They are good models for reviews, social media post, or chat log analyses. This research work analyzes the effectiveness of BiLSTM for sentiment-driven decision-making, in real-time analysis of feedback, and customer engagement based on their personalized characteristics. As shown in the results section, although the model excelled at positivity detection, limitations with neutrality and negativity detection existed, attributed to imbalances within the dataset. Some integration concerns and scalability challenges along with some ethical issues concerning the algorithms like mitigating bias have been analyzed. The research offers a systematic framework to deploy BiLSTM towards customer-centric innovation.

articleTitle: Advancing Techniques for Deepfake Detection and Evaluation: Challenges and Innovations
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: The proliferation of deepfakes-also termed artificial intelligence-generated synthetic media poses unprecedented challenges to the digital authenticity of media, for media integrity, and to societies’ trust in its credibility. Despite such significant technological advancements, current methodologies for detecting deepfakes remain somewhat fragmented, reactive, and often unable to keep pace with rapidly evolving technologies in generative AI. This article considers a comprehensive multi-modal approach toward deepfake detection by integrating an advanced machine learning algorithm, novel statistical correlation techniques, and forensic image analysis that would fill in the critical gaps in the existing frameworks. By using an extensive dataset of 10,000 synthetic and authentic media samples from diverse domains, we developed a hybrid neural network architecture that attained 94.3% accuracy on identifying AI-generated content. Our methodology utilized ensemble learning by combining spatial-temporal inconsistency detection, biological signal analysis, and advanced feature extraction algorithms. Key findings demonstrate significant vulnerabilities in current deepfake generation models, with our proposed technique successfully identifying subtle artifacts and inconsistencies across multiple generative AI platforms. This research conclusively demonstrates that proactive, adaptive detection strategies are critical to mitigating the potential risks associated with synthetic media, providing a robust framework for future technological interventions in digital forensics and media authentication.

articleTitle: Enhanced Handover Management in 5G Networks using Machine Learning in Fading Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: This study explores the use of machine learning (ML) to improve initial handover performance for 5G networks by analysing fading-affected scenarios. In this study, we assess the ability of ML models to predict optimal handover decisions compared with conventional methods. In this study, simulation results show that our ML-based methods can reduce the handover inaccuracy by 50%, decrease latency up to 10 times and stabilize network performance. We accompany our assessment with a series of graphical analyses to show how ML algorithms change their behaviour dynamically in response to deteriorating link intensity due user mobility and increasing h/o frequency, thereby degrading the network performance. The results clearly illustrate that ML enabled handover optimization is significantly more effective than traditional methods in accommodating fading-channel dynamics, thereby improving both the network performance and user experience of future generation wireless networks.

articleTitle: Fraud Call Detection using Pre-Data Feeding Method by Financial Institution
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: Fraudulent calls have become a pervasive threat, leading to significant financial losses and compromising the security of individuals and organizations. This project focuses on the development of a fraud call detection site aimed at combating these malicious activities and preventing financial fraud. Leveraging advanced technologies such as machine learning and anomaly detection, the site is designed to accurately identify and block fraudulent calls in real-time. The project encompasses extensive research on existing detection methodologies, the implementation of a user-friendly interface for reporting and monitoring suspicious activities, and the integration of robust algorithms to enhance detection accuracy. By providing an effective tool for detecting fraudulent calls, this project aims to reduce the incidence of financial fraud, protect potential victims, and contribute to a safer communication environment. The outcomes of this project are expected to offer valuable insights and practical solutions in the ongoing battle against fraud in the telecommunications sector.

articleTitle: Low Light Image Enhancement: A Special Click
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: Photography and images are an important and integral part of today’s world, resulting in the development of multimedia and many other subjects comparable to image processing. The specifications of the camera and camera lens are just not enough hence image processing is always required. Low light photography, the problem gets even bigger because the camera lens fails to capture enough light and hence low light photography depends mostly upon image processing algorithms which help to reduce noise in the image, brighten the image for better overall visual quality and enlighten the hidden dark areas. Many efforts have been put into advancing image quality in little light, but none have given satisfactory results. This research report aims to analyses the techniques used for low- light image improvement and what advancements can be made to advance the image condition further.

articleTitle: Energy-efficient edge based intrusion detection system using machine learning
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: Edge based computing’s primary goal is to enhance network performance by storing and processing data in proximity to the end user. However, the rapid development of edge computing often overlooks security risks in powerful applications and large-scale computer systems. Security and privacy are essential prerequisites for both edge computing and the ecosystems built around it. Additionally, intrusion detection systems (IDS) are used to detect and analyze network traffic, identify anomalies, trigger alarms, and automatically block the traffic according to the sets of rules design in IDS. This paper discusses the Edge based IDS designed specifically for edge computing with accuracy 99.77% to detect the attacks with 30% of malicious electric vehicle include in the simulation focusing on its relevant processes, features, and procedures.

articleTitle: Advanced Medical Question and Answering Chatbot Powered by Llama-2 For Precis Health Answer
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: LLaMA-2 model, which is known for having the best capabilities in natural language processing at the core of our system. With respect to symptom diagnosis, it ranked among the most accurate in being able to give the chances of as many conditions possible as per the information that it receives from the user. Creating custom responses to unique user queries all the time, which may potentially increase user satisfaction and engagement. We have tested and perfected our chatbot to ensure that the capabilities stood out at a level of accuracy as high as 85 percent-showing outstanding care in the matters of healthcare assistance issues under numerous medical topics. Our work adds advanced features with the improvement techniques to the conventional medical Q and A chatbot. The new deep learning chatbot is not only great for symptom diagnosis but also uses its capabilities to provide context-aware responses based on user health history, lifestyles, and preferences with adjustment of its advice for a more personal healthcare experience.

articleTitle: Analysis of Cloud Service Providers and Computing Services in Modem IT Infrastructure
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: In recent years, a growth of cloud computing services has revolutionized modern IT infrastructure and left organizations with difficult choices of what service provider to use and how to implement such services. Much research is done on the level of individual cloud services, yet an important gap still exists with regard to comprehensive comparative analyses that evaluate major cloud service providers across multiple dimensions. This research systematically assesses market leaders: Amazon Web Services (AWS), Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud Platform (GCP)—by taking into account their computing services, pricing models, metrics for performance, and security frameworks. Utilizing a mixed methods approach, we analyzed the available quantitative performance data of 2,500 cloud deployments across 12 regions from all over the world, in addition to carrying out qualitative assessments by structured interviews with 150 IT decision-makers. Our results have large differences in service reliability (±15%), cost-effectiveness (23% variance in similar workloads), and integration capabilities across providers. Of course, in compute-intensive workloads, AWS did better, but in integrating enterprises, Azure won, and in machine learning, one could see clear advantages with GCP. The study concludes that optimal cloud service selection is workload-specific rather than provider-centric, so that organizations can benefit from the multi-cloud strategy. Such insights define a decision frame for organizations that are using or planning to adopt cloud services, thereby contributing to the growing body of knowledge in cloud computing infrastructure management.

articleTitle: Enhanced Coffee Bean Defect Detection Using Super-Resolution GANs and Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: Image Super-Resolution (SR) is a key challenge in computer vision, focusing on enhancing low-resolution images while preserving details. This paper presents a novel method using Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) for improving image quality, specifically targeting coffee bean defect detection. The proposed SR-GAN model includes a generator that upscales low-resolution inputs and a discriminator that differentiates between generated high-resolution images and real ones. Trained on a coffee bean dataset, the model optimizes loss functions to balance perceptual quality and fidelity, capturing subtle defects like cracks and discolorations. Enhanced images are processed by two Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs): one identifies broad defect categories, such as defective black beans, brown beans, broken beans and non-defective high-quality beans. This layered approach ensures more precise defect identification and classification, overcoming limitations of previous methods that struggled with subtle defects. Performance evaluations show that SR-GAN and CNN significantly outperforms existing models in resolution enhancement and classification accuracy, offering a robust solution for improving quality control in coffee production.

articleTitle: Continual Learning Techniques to Reduce Forgetting: A Comparative Study
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: A key aspect of artificial intelligence is continual learning. The capacity of a model to incrementally learn from a new task and adapt to it without losing the previous knowledge. A fundamental challenge that comes to successful continual learning is catastrophic forgetting; while learning a new task the model forgets the previously learned tasks. Various approaches to mitigate forgetting and enhance continual learning have been discussed across benchmark datasets such as MNIST, CIFAR- 10, and Permuted MNIST. we focus mainly on replay, regularization, and modular architecture-based methods to prevent forgetting. Regularization methods penalize the significant change in parameters during the learning of new tasks while maintaining crucial parameters of previously completed tasks. Replay-based methods store samples of earlier tasks in explicit memory or generate pseudo-samples with the help of generative models. Modular architecture-based methods partition the neural architecture into task-specific modules to prevent interference between tasks, to effectively address catastrophic forgetting. This paper presents a comparative study of the key continual learning methods that reduce catastrophic forgetting. The findings demonstrate the trade-offs between different methods. We examine the efficiency and effectiveness of each method and propose a hybrid technique to prevent catastrophic forgetting. Our comparative analysis emphasizes the significance of choosing the best method depending on the specific requirement of the learning environment, the task complexity, and resource constraints.

articleTitle: Beyond Poverty: Identifying the Overlooked Factors Influencing Education
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: Poverty is the most critical factor hindering quality education for students all over the world and sustaining a vicious cycle of inequity. Poverty affects over 700 million people worldwide and causes a deep impact on students learning. Education, a widely accepted means of breaking poverty, is pivotal to the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs): 1-No Poverty and 4-Quality Education. Keeping these goals in mind, this work explores the correlation between poverty and education, focusing on the socioeconomic linkages, challenges of resource scarcity and many more. The paper discovers 16 socioeconomic factors, in addition to financial factors that affect students’ academics. The work also proposes strategies with special emphasis on improved access, inclusion, and learning outcomes, through past literature, and by leveraging machine learning algorithms: Random Forest and XGBoost.

articleTitle: A Fine-Tuned DenseNet-Based Diagnosis Approach for Multi-Class Breast Cancer Classification
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: Breast cancer is a prevalent tumor across women and is associated with a high mortality rate. Prompt diagnosis is one of the biggest challenges that needs to be addressed globally, as it can considerably improve survival rates. An automatic diagnosis system based on deep learning models is critical for improving detection, prediction accuracy, and survivability. This study used various DenseNet-based architectures for multi-class classification using the BUSI dataset. The experiments indicate that the fine-tuned DenseNet201 model outperforms with an accuracy of 98.28%. The results demonstrate the promising capability of the fine-tuned DenseNet201 model to have a high potential for further implementation in practice for achieving early diagnosis and highly individualized approaches for better treatment. The further development of extensive and diverse data sets will be essential for developing new diagnostic methods and improving the existing ones.

articleTitle: White-Box Adversarial Exploitation of NIDS: Insights from FGSM, PGD, and C&W
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: Network Intrusion Detection Systems (NIDS) help in detecting harmful activities and malicious activities by keeping an eye on network traffic or system for malignant activity. However, studies have found that Network Intrusion Detection Systems (NIDS) can be tricked by making tiny often invisible changes to the input data known as adversarial attacks to confuse machine learning models and cause them to make wrong decisions. This paper explores how different types of adversarial attacks affect NIDS models, focusing on techniques like Fast Gradient sign Method (FGSM), Projected Gradient Descent (PGD), and the Carlini and Wagner (C&W) attack. This work contributes by assessing how these adversarial attacks affect the NIDS model by analyzing three key metrics: precision, recall, and F1 score. These metrics were analyzed to evaluate how successful the adversarial attacks were and how they affected the performance of the NIDS. Experimental results demonstrate that these adversarial attacks significantly degrade the performance of NIDS, particularly in terms of precision and overall detection capability. FGSM was able to reduce the accuracy of NIDS from 73.01% to 53.92% as epsilon (ϵ) value increased from 0.1 to 0.5, while PGD was able to reduce it to 19.63%. The C&W attack, with the confidence parameter set to 1, resulted in 55.20% accuracy, highlighting the model's vulnerability to adversarial attacks. This research highlights the vulnerabilities of NIDS to adversarial attacks and provides a detailed analysis of the challenges posed by such threats in cybersecurity, emphasizing the need for advanced mitigation techniques to address them.

articleTitle: Speech Signal Enhancement Using CNN-Driven Encoder-Decoder Architectures for Reverberation Mitigation
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: There can be lots of challenges in the signal quality due to reverberation noise. This noise badly effects the signal to noise ratio and sound quality. This research article proposes a convolutional neural network (CNN) based encoder decoder structure to address the problem of speech signal with reverberations. This model uses the hierarchical feature extraction ability of CNNs to learn and localise the reverberant contents from speech signals. On the basis of a number of experiments, this method is proved to be more effective than traditional ones. It is very useful in upgrading the speech signals, and also provides a good performance under different conditions which makes it useful for practical uses in communication systems and hearing aids.

articleTitle: An improved energy optimization model for sensitive IoT devices using clustered machine learning
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: The rise of the Internet of Things (IoT) has been emphasized in range-sensitive devices like medical sensors and environmental monitors, which need durable battery life alongside reliable performance. However, the limited resources of these devices make energy optimization especially difficult. Current energy optimization models for IoT devices often use simplistic techniques that might only partially capture these devices' diverse range of energy profiles. In this paper, an enhanced machine learning-based optimization model is designed for clustered energy conservation to manage the AEC vulnerabilities of IoT devices. The model employs a clustering method to group the devices with similar energy usage patterns, which helps better predict and optimize total load across clusters. The model also uses machine learning algorithms to evolve with usage patterns and change energy optimization strategies accordingly. This strategy has been applied to a wide range of low-power IoT devices. It has shown substantial savings in energy utilization, making them much more efficient than conventional optimization methods. In conclusion, we argue how our design enables scalable and customizable solutions for energy-efficient maintenance of IoT devices running sensitive computations. We use machine learning and clustering techniques that are custom-built for the energy management of these devices, ensuring long battery life and reliable performance even under heavy workloads or critical applications. This may also accelerate the adoption and evolution of those security IoT devices across different areas, increasing their effects on society.

articleTitle: A Sensitive Collision Avoidance System Improved for Terrain Navigation on Elevated Terrain
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: This study introduces a specialized Collision Avoidance System designed specifically for navigating hilly terrains. It incorporates machine learning algorithms seamlessly integrated into an Arduino platform to improve safety measures by identifying potential collisions in challenging topographies. By harnessing machine learning methodologies, the system can detect and forecast obstacles in real-time, providing timely alerts and enabling proactive maneuvers to prevent collisions. The incorporation of Arduino technology streamlines the implementation process, offering a cost-efficient and adaptable solution tailored for hilly environments. Rigorous experimental assessments confirm the effectiveness and dependability of the proposed Collision Avoidance System, highlighting its potential to elevate safety standards in dynamic and intricate terrains.

articleTitle: Development of Oral Cancer Detection Technique: A Comprehensive Approach Using CNNs and TensorFlow Lite
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: Oral Cancer has been a great threat to many, working as a silent predator, oral cancer in one of the leading contributors in overall cancer stats. Improving patient outcomes requires early diagnosis and screening, but access to prompt and efficient diagnostic techniques is still restricted, especially in environments with limited resources. The creation and incorporation of a convolutional neural network (CNN)-based model for oral cancer detection into a mobile application is shown in this research. This model, which was developed with TensorFlow and tuned for TensorFlow Lite deployment, makes oral cancer screening accessible, affordable, and real-time. The architecture of the model is specifically engineered to detect early indications of malignancy with exceptional precision, thereby substantially reducing the obstacles to efficient mouth cancer screening. This tool could significantly improve oral cancer outcomes worldwide by incorporating cutting-edge machine learning techniques into common technology, making it a vital step in the fight against this fatal illness.

articleTitle: Transforming Oral Healthcare Using Machine Learning Technique
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: This work proposes new methodologies through an AI prediction model for timely diagnosis of oral cancer which leads to better prognosis and survival rates for individuals with this disease. It sews the current loopholes in existing work by incorporating diversified, real-time, authentic and validated data set that will be used to train the model, along with optimizing the model which greatly enhances the prediction rate and accuracy of the model. Central to this methodology is the development of a user-friendly, app-based tool that simplifies and accelerates the diagnostic process. This technology, which is intended for use by both the public and healthcare professionals, provides an affordable option that improves accessibility to prompt diagnosis, especially for marginalized communities. This instrument is a crucial asset in the fight against oral cancer because of its high accuracy and ease of use, which may also improve patient outcomes and lower total healthcare expenditures.

articleTitle: A MultiResUNet-based Deep Learning Architecture for Accurate Lung Segmentation in Chest X-Rays
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: Accurate chest X-ray segmentation (CXR) is vital for disease diagnosis and monitoring, such as Covid-19. This study proposes an advanced deep learning-based framework for enhanced CXR segmentation incorporating a multi-resolution methodology to improve lung segmentation accuracy. We experimented on a dataset of 3616 COVID-19 images and their corresponding segmentation masks from the COVID-19 Radiography Database, evaluating different state-of-the-art models. The results demonstrated that the proposed MultiResUNet outperforms existing methods with faster convergence and an accuracy of 99.52%. The results show that the proposed MultiResUNet model improves the accuracy and precision of CXR segmentation, especially for detecting COVID-19, and enables the development of more robust AI-driven tools in medical image analysis.

articleTitle: Optimizing DDoS Attack Detection Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: The increase in the Distributed Denial of Service attack (DDoS) leads to a significant threat to the network security. Inability to timely and accurately detect DDoS attacks disrupts services offered by companies and the government causing financial losses. Additionally, prolonged DDoS attacks can spoil user experience and degrade company reputation. The recent literature reveals various techniques for detecting DDoS attacks, including pre-trained machine learning and deep learning algorithms. This research paper addresses this challenge by tweaking random forest algorithms for maximum accuracy using CICDDoS2019 dataset. The methodology includes collecting of dataset, data processing, feature scaling and training multiple machine learning algorithms to identify maximum accuracy for detecting DDoS attacks. The result shows improvement of accuracy and precision of machine learning models used. Future work may include training the model for other types of attacks, real time implementation of the model developed, developing a hybrid approach for detection and protection from DDoS attack.

articleTitle: Deep Learning for Detection and Morphological Analysis of Stomatal Complexes in Microscopic Imaging
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: The accurate detection and classification of stomatal complexes play a critical role in understanding plant physiology, particularly in areas such as gas exchange regulation and water conservation. Leveraging advancements in computer vision and deep learning, this study introduces a robust framework for the automated identification and morphological analysis of stomata cells within microscopic images. A large annotated dataset was utilized to train and evaluate a deep learning model capable of localizing stomatal complexes with high precision. Employing advanced object detection architectures, our model achieved high performance metrics, demonstrating its efficacy in distinguishing stomatal regions from surrounding epidermal cells. The developed system not only facilitates rapid and accurate detection but also contributes to improved morphological analysis, allowing re-searchers to quantitatively assess stomatal features under various conditions. This approach promises significant contributions to plant sciences, providing a scalable tool for cellular analysis that may inform studies on plant adaptation, environmental stress response, and crop improvement. Our findings illustrate the potential of integrating computer vision with biological research, setting a precedent for future work in automated plant cell analysis.

articleTitle: Employing Vision Transformer for Monocular Depth Estimation
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: Monocular depth estimation (MDE) is an important task in computer vision, it enables a range of applications like robotic navigation, augmented reality and also used in surgical guidance. This paper shows the use of ViTs for MDE and focuses on the Depth Anything V2(DA-V2) model. DA-V2 model leverages a teacher-student training approach and uses the synthetic and unlabeled real images which are designed to enhance the accuracy of depth estimation. DA-V2 is fine-tuned on EndoSLAM dataset and contains challenging visual scenes from endoscopic images of the stomach, colon and small intestine to check the adaptability of the model to medical depth estimation. Our experiment shows that the fine-tuned DA-V2 outperforms all the conventional models like Endo-SfMLearner and achieves reductions in root mean squared error(RMSE) and absolute relative error, across all anatomical datasets. DA-V2 achieves the RMSE values 1.245, 1.028, and 2.021 for the stomach, colon, and intestine datasets, respectively as compared to the SfMLearner’s 6.387, 6.657, and 14.787. The findings show that ViTs are capable of achieving higher accuracy and generalization in monocular depth estimation tasks. This study highlights the effectiveness of DA-V2 and Vision Transformers in Monocular Depth Estimation and opens up possibilities for further model optimization.

articleTitle: Adaptive Fuzzy Logic Framework for Threat Detection in Distributed Honeypot Systems Leveraging Blockchain Technology
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: In the continuous expanding domain of cybersecurity, the rise of more cyber threats is also increasing. Therefore, it demands the development of more efficient defense strategies. In past, honeypots are used as lucrative devices to attract malicious activity. However, most of the honeypot systems are static in nature, which may not be efficient in distributed environment. This paper introduces a Dynamic Distributed Honeypot System (DDHS) for the same purpose. In these honeypots nodes are dynamically distributed and connected via blockchain technology, aimed at improving threat detection and response capabilities. By distributing honeypots across multiple nodes in a blockchain network, the proposed system is more secure against external attack. This paper discusses the dynamic fuzzy rules method for the threat detection in the distributed honeypot systems.

articleTitle: Deep Defense: A Hybrid LSTM-ANN Architecture for Intelligent Intrusion Detection System
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: The rapidly evolving cyber threat landscape requires innovative and adaptive intrusion detection solutions. Traditional signature-based intrusion detection systems, despite their high accuracy, are inherently inflexible and susceptible to evasion tactics, making them ineffective against novel and sophisticated attacks. In contrast, machine learning-powered anomaly-based intrusion detection systems demonstrate improved detection capabilities, but their advantages are often outweighed by substantial drawbacks, including significant computational resource requirements when the dataset and its features for behavior analysis increase. Also, there are high power consumption and latency issues in communication that compromise network performance. This study proposes a hybrid ANN-LSTM approach for performing deep packet inspection and efficiently detecting malicious network packets. By analyzing binary container data, our model reduces time and space complexity, thereby mitigating the computational resources and power consumption challenges but also increasing the efficiency of intrusion detection by 3%, making it more intelligent than various established IDS.

articleTitle: Exploring Factors Using Statistical Approach to Analyse Purchase Intention for Electronic Products: A UTAUT-Based SEM Perspective
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: The research paper aims to examine and understand the determinants that impact user behaviour and intention when utilizing e-commerce applications to purchase electronic products using the conceptual framework. UTAUT model is employed as the research framework for this research. This theory examines the application of consumers and their purchase Intention for various electronic products applicable. This study examines EE, PE, FC, and SI's predictive role in Behavioural Intention and User Behaviour. The research study also studies the moderating role of task anxiety on Behavioural Intention to Purchase. The study found that PE increases users' propensity to buy electronics on e-commerce apps. EE strongly influences users' intentions, emphasizing the need for user-friendly interfaces.

articleTitle: Toxic Comments Classification using Machine Learning and Word Embedding Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: Toxic comments are comments which are disrespectful, unreasonable and infuriating that make the reading uncomfortable. Sometimes these comments are inappropriate and not good for the public. These comments make daily content consumers uncomfortable and sometime even cause emotional as well as emotional harm. There are some people whose purpose for coming online is to create trouble for others and make their work and daily life difficult by making inappropriate comments. This kind of behavior can be described as anti-social and harmful to society. Many steps have already been taken to catch these troublemakers and punish them accordingly by blocking users who are found guilty. This cannot be done personally by checking one by one, to achieve this purpose we need to make a model. We have applied three Machine Learning Models logistic regression, Naive bayes, SVM and three Word Embedding Techniques, Word2Vec, FastText and Glove which can classify comments, and the content creator take appropriate action against users who makes these comments by reporting and even by deleting their account if needed. Out of all six techniques SVM has outperformed for classification of toxic and non-toxic comments and normal text classification in general. SVM gives the best results with 93.61% accuracy and F1 score of 93%. Proposed technique has improvised accuracy score as compared to existing techniques.

articleTitle: Vision-Based Hand Gesture Recognition System for Assistive Communication Using Neural Networks and GSM Integration
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: This paper explores the application of vision-based hand gesture recognition in addressing communication challenges faced by deaf and dumb individuals within the realm of human-computer interaction (HCI). Highlighting the barriers posed by conventional communication methods and sign language interpretation, the paper introduces the Dumb Aid Phone system as an innovative solution. This system, functioning as an interface, enables seamless interaction for non-speaking individuals with their surroundings. Utilizing image processing and neural networking, the system captures and interprets hand gestures, matching them with a database to generate corresponding speech sounds. Enhanced by a web camera and a GSM module, the Dumb Aid Phone system not only facilitates effective communication but also holds the potential to revolutionize accessibility, contributing to a more inclusive society for the deaf and dumb community.

articleTitle: Augmented Reality in Education: Enhancing Learning Experiences
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: The integration of Augmented Reality (AR) into learning environments is still an area of significant challenge in light of increasingly dynamic technological landscapes. Whereas the traditional methods of learning do not appeal much to digitally native learners, the existing gap in terms of the systematic improvement of outcomes lies in the understanding of immersive technologies. This paper combines both quantitative assessments of learning and qualitative phenomenological analyses from three different educational settings: schools at the secondary level, institutions of higher learning, and professional training centers. Through an effective intervention involving 742 participants using cutting-edge AR learning platforms, our study has revealed significant cognitive and engagement-related improvements. The groups experiencing AR-enhanced curricula showed a 37% increase in knowledge retention, as well as 42% higher engagement rates, along with significantly improved spatial reasoning abilities. Qualitative data further support the idea that motivation improves, as participants indicated better conceptual understanding and greater independence in learning. The findings indicate that AR is transformative in educational practice, making it simple to bring theoretical knowledge and experiential learning together. Here, the merging of digital information with the students' physical learning environment is not merely a technological intervention, but a fundamental redesign of pedagogical approaches that promises a more interactive, personalized, and immersive education paradigm.

articleTitle: Managing Economic Load Dispatch through Multi-swarm Statistical Particle Swarm Optimization
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: In power systems, the ELD is crucial for managing the minimum generation cost of electrical-generating units while fulfilling the constraints and maintaining the load demand. Traditional optimization techniques do not provide an optimum solution for nonlinear, large, and complex ELD data. This study proposed a multiswarm statistical particle swarm optimization algorithm for solving the ELD problem. This paper presents a multiswarm statistical particle swarm optimization algorithm to solve nonlinear and complex ELD problems. Multi-swarm statistical particle swarm optimization (MSPSO) is a new and strong type of PSO that uses multiple swarms and statistical adaptation mechanisms to improve swarm exploration and convergence in search spaces. This makes MSPSO a good way to solve difficult nonlinear ELD problems. This work considered two case studies of 10 and 15 generatinlg unit data to examine the performance of MSPSO in terms of minimization of cost, speed of convergence, and computation time. The results obtained by MSPSO for both case studies were compared with those of the other optimization techniques. The results shown by MSPSO are better than those of the others.

Author Keywords: Multi-swarm Statistical Particle Swarm Optimization (MSPSO) algorithm

articleTitle: Data Protection in Enhanced EXplainable Digital Twins: Insights from Hybrid AI
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: Deep Learning (DL) based artificial intelligence (AI) is becoming pervasive in almost all the day to day applications. These DL algorithms require large amounts of data, which can be easily collected nowadays by deploying sensors in the environment of the system under observation. These DL algorithms however, suffer from drawbacks such as being criticised as ‘black-boxes’, being biased to generating predictions based on past data and ignoring the human expertise. Hence, an architecture of Enhanced eXplainable Digital Twins (EXDTs) was proposed. EXDTs remove ‘black-boxness’ of DL algorithms by using the XAI approaches. Further, the digital twins (DTs) underlying the EXDTs are constructed through the sensor data and depict the real-time simulatability. Also, to improve the explainability and use the human expertise/ experience, EXDTs use the domain experts’ qualitative data. EXDTs are a class of Hybrid AI systems, that use the numeric data for underlying DL algorithms and subjective knowledge of the domain expert. This multimodal data in EXDTs opens up new attacks fronts for data manipulation and change the EXDTs’ outputs. In this manuscript, we discuss about the data protection in EXDTs, by simulating various types of attacks and suggesting possible ways the system can counter them. We feel our proposed framework is useful for the involved stakeholders in various domains like precision agriculture, healthcare, manufacturing, etc.

articleTitle: Live Audio Recognition and Text Conversion System
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: With the advancement of technologies, different methods are currently being used for converting spoken language into text. These systems offer a hands-free alternative to traditional input methods, especially for individuals with physical disabilities or those requiring efficient documentation of spoken content. The goal of this study is to review recent advancements in this field and highlight gaps in current research, with a focus on accuracy, language adaptability, ease of use, and the integration of various technologies. We also suggest future directions for enhancing and developing this technology further.

articleTitle: Enhancing the Security of Healthcare Data in Cloud Computing Environments
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: Cloud computing has completely evolved the way health care data is managed, but it also introduces critical security vulnerabilities that can compromise the privacy of patient information and threaten regulatory compliance. Herein, we present one of the most severe challenges: securing EHRs in a cloud environment with access to data while maintaining HIPAA compliance. We introduce a novel hybrid framework combining homomorphic encryption with blockchain-based access control and dynamic audit logging. The framework was used with a three-phase experimental approach and was deployed over five major healthcare institutions while being analyzed for 2.3 million patient records over 18 months. Results showed a high success rate of 99.97% against denial-of-service attacks while showing reductions in latency time about data retrieval up to 34% compared to traditional methods of encryption. Security-incident-based variation was reduced up to 78%, and 99.99% data integrity was achieved during concurrent access scenarios. Cost analysis shows that overheads in security management amount to a reduction of 45% against conventional systems. Our results show that the proposed framework is far better for healthcare data security, along with improved operational efficiency and regulatory compliance. This work contributes to the literature by providing a scalable and cost-efficient solution addressing the most complex security requirements of modern health care systems in cloud environments. The fact that the framework is implemented successfully in real life seems to reflect its effectiveness for mass-scale implementation in health organizations.

articleTitle: Model for Movie Recommendation System using Collaborative Filtering and Content-Based Filtering Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: Recommendation systems are widely used to help users find relevant content based on their interests. This research focuses on creating a Movie Recommendation System using Collaborative Filtering and Content-Based Filtering techniques. The goal is to improve the accuracy and relevance of recommendations while addressing challenges like limited user data and new user scenarios. Collaborative filtering predicts a user’s preferences by analyzing the preferences of similar users. Content-based filtering recommends movies by comparing their features, such as genres, actors, and directors, to the user’s preferences. A hybrid approach is also explored, combining both techniques to improve the overall performance of the system. The system uses the MovieLens dataset, which contains user ratings and movie details. The accuracy and effectiveness of the system are measured using metrics like RMSE and Precision. The results show that the hybrid model provides better recommendations compared to using only one technique. This study shows how advanced recommendation techniques can make movie streaming platforms more user-friendly. It also suggests ideas for future work, such as including real-time data and user feedback to enhance recommendations further.

articleTitle: Simplifying code translation: Custom syntax language to C language transpiler
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: In today’s world, programming has become a very essential skill as it is used everywhere, from creating software’s for operating systems to analysis of patients’ health care data in biomedical engineering. Programmers usually face a lot of difficulties to understand beginner level coding languages having low-level syntax. The proposed study "Simplifying Code Translation: Custom Syntax Language to C Language Transpiler", targets the specified problem and provides the solution in a form of transpiler that converts the newly developed custom language (made up of high-level syntax) to C language. The developed tool minimizes the overall cost incurred during the code designing process. This transpiler consists of 4 main parts: preprocessor, lexer, parser and emitter. It first starts by creating preprocessor which handles preprocessor directives such as 'define' and 'include'. This preprocessed code is then passed onto lexer which tokenizes the code. The parser is responsible for creating Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) using the tokens provided. The final AST is then transformed to C program by the emitter. Then output C code maintains proper syntactic and semantic structure of the original custom syntax language code.

articleTitle: Real-Time Sign Language Recognition and Translation Using MediaPipe and Random Forests for Inclusive Communication
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: Communication barriers faced by deaf and speech-impaired individuals necessitate innovative solutions for effective interaction with the hearing community. This research proposes a novel approach to sign language recognition and translation by leveraging Random Forests and MediaPipe technology. MediaPipe facilitates real-time hand gesture tracking and extraction of hand landmarks crucial for sign language interpretation. Subsequently, a Random Forest classifier is employed to recognize the signs depicted by the tracked gestures accurately. Upon successful recognition, the system seamlessly translates the sign language into written words and text, fostering enhanced communication accessibility for the deaf and speech-impaired community. Integrating advanced machine learning techniques with real-time tracking technology offers promising avenues for breaking down communication barriers and promoting inclusivity.

articleTitle: Real-Time Yoga Pose Recognition and Correction Feedback System Using Deep Learning and Computer Vision
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: Yoga pose detection is a rapidly evolving field that integrates advanced technology with wellness, addressing the need for accurate and adaptable systems for diverse user groups. This paper proposes a novel framework that combines RGB images, depth maps, and skeletal joint data to enhance multi-modal feature extraction and improve spatial-temporal analysis for tasks such as action recognition and human activity modeling. The framework overcomes challenges such as pose variations and occlusions through techniques like data augmentation, model optimization, and robust performance evaluation. Experimental results demonstrate the system’s high accuracy of 91.7%, successfully detecting six distinct yoga pose sequences in real time and providing self-correction feedback to users, thereby improving performance. The practical applications of this approach are significant, with potential use cases in yoga studios, fitness centers, and home environments, promoting scalable, precise, and globally accessible yoga practices.

articleTitle: Enhancing Flood Severity Prediction through a Combined Threshold-Based Alert Algorithm and Random Forest Classifier
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: Flooding is a significant and recurrent issue that poses severe risks to communities, economies, and environments. Traditional flood prediction methods, which often rely on fixed thresholds, may lack adaptability to changing conditions. Meanwhile, machine learning (ML) models like Random Forest Classifiers (RFCs) offer advanced predictive capabilities, but may not provide straightforward alert mechanisms. This research proposes a novel approach that integrates a Threshold-Based Alert Algorithm (TBA) with an RFC to enhance flood severity prediction. The combined model leverages the strengths of both methodologies: immediate, interpretable alerts from the TBA and adaptive, data-driven insights from the RFC. Using historical and real-time data from river basins in Wisconsin and New York, the hybrid model demonstrates improved accuracy and reliability over traditional methods and standalone RFCs. The results indicate that this integrated approach offers a more effective tool for flood management and disaster mitigation.

articleTitle: Cloud Computing in Enhancing the Efficiency and Integration of Alternative Energy Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: In response to growing environmental concerns and the need for sustainable development, alternative energy systems have emerged as crucial solutions to the problems associated with fossil fuels. This research focuses on the significant role cloud computing plays in improving the efficiency and integration of various alternative energy systems such as solar, wind, hydropower, biomass, geothermal, and tidal/wave energy. The study explores how cloud computing technologies enable real-time data processing, storage, and analysis of the large datasets generated by these renewable energy sources, thus optimizing their performance and integration into the energy grid. Cloud computing provides advanced data management tools that are vital for managing the variable and intermittent nature of renewable energy production. By utilizing cloud-based platforms, energy producers can achieve improved forecasting, load balancing, and energy distribution, which are essential for enhancing efficiency and reliability. Additionally, this research highlights how cloud computing fosters collaboration and innovation by offering a scalable and flexible infrastructure. This infrastructure supports the development of new technologies and applications within the renewable energy sector, promoting continuous advancements and breakthroughs. This research underscores the crucial role of cloud computing in advancing a sustainable energy future.

articleTitle: A Machine Learning Framework For Efficient Malware Detection and Classification
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: Malware detection is a very important aspect of cybersecurity, it is the act of monitoring computer systems, networks and/or data to identify malicious software (malware) such as viruses and ransomware in addition to spyware or phishing threats. As malware continues to evolve, more traditional methods such as signature-based and heuristic detection are often inadequate, especially against the ever-increasing number of new and sophisticated threats, zero-day attacks. This has in turn paved the way for the rise of machine learning (ML) as a more flexible and efficient solution. This is where machine learning comes into play; specialized algorithms, trained on extensive datasets, can identify intricate patterns and behaviours that elude traditional systems. Unlike signature-based systems which depend upon identifiable markers of known malware, ML can more thoroughly examine characteristics like network traffic, file behaviour, and API calls to find even novel or altered malware classifications. The detection accuracy was improved by a number of artificial techniques, including Decision Trees, SVM and Random Forests, lowering the rate of false positives. In this process, feature engineering has a significant impact. With this analysis based on multiple features like system calls, file signatures and network patterns ML models can make accurate predictions. Understanding malware requires techniques such as static analysis (investigating file code) and dynamic analysis (watching behaviour). Collectively, these developments combine to make ML an effective method of detecting both existing and new threats.

articleTitle: Evolution and Future Trends in Wireless Communication: From 2G to 6G Technologies
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: The journey from 2G to emerging 6G is impressive, mirroring the long evolutionary path of wireless communication technology. We address critical transitions in cellular networks in light of architectural transformation, performance metrics, and the enablers of new technologies. Key trends identified: from Kbps data rate growth exponentially in 2G to Tbps in 6G; a fall of latency from the 500-ms level to sub-millisecond latency; and more importantly, from human-centric communication to machine-centric communication. It will bring some breakthrough technologies, like terahertz communications, intelligent reflecting surfaces, and quantum computing integration, revolutionizing the network configuration and capability. 6G networks will highlight many unprecedented applications such as holographic communications and extended reality; however, that is not possible without addressing various challenges related to spectrum efficiency, energy optimization, and security challenges. This report synthesized technical literature, standardization documents, and industry insights to propose a roadmap of future wireless networks with innovative and AI-integrated spectrum utilization concepts and sustainable designs. The results are critical to researchers, policymakers, and industry stakeholders in the shaping of the next generation of wireless communication systems.

articleTitle: IoT-Enabled Smart Classrooms for Enhanced Learning Environments
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: Innovative integration of digital infrastructure with pedagogical practices in rapidly transforming educational environments.
