The technology is well recognized yet fails to solve issues in traditional classrooms due to poor resource management, less individualized learning experiences, and real-time performance monitoring. The research focuses on these issues and answers them by designing and implementing an IoT-enabled smart classroom ecosystem aiming at changing the learning environment. Developed an end-to-end IoT framework that incorporates sensor networks, machine learning algorithms, and adaptive learning interfaces across multiple educational institutions using a mixed-method approach. This included prototype development, systematic data collection, and iterative performance analysis using advanced analytics and user experience assessments. Significant learning engagement improvements by 23.7%. Resource usage efficiency improves by 35.2%. Excellent Personalized learning results, Real-time environmental monitoring of the IoT system, Adaptive instructional strategy with the complete track record of the student. The precision control in climate through sensors for an optimum lighting effect Smart management of the space using sensors. In sum, our research establishes a transformative model for technology-enhanced educational spaces, providing a scalable blueprint for future smart learning environments where technological innovation is integrated into pedagogical effectiveness.

articleTitle: SUBIINA: Stress and Unhappiness Behavioural Identification using Intelligent Artificial Neural Networks and Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: This paper presents an overview of recent research on stress detection using speech and facial expression analysis. The utilization of speech and facial expressions for the purpose of stress detection has garnered considerable interest in recent times, largely due to their non-invasive and cost-effective characteristics. The paper provides a brief introduction to the physiological and psychological aspects of stress and how it affects speech and facial production. Various approaches to stress detection using speech and facial expression analysis are discussed, including acoustic, prosodic, linguistic, and visual features. The paper also discusses the challenges associated with stress detection using speech and facial expression analysis and potential applications of this technology. In conclusion, the paper discusses future research directions in this domain, which include the creation of stress detection models that are even more precise and dependable, as well as their integration into real-world applications.

articleTitle: Smart Traffic Management for Emergency Response through IoT Integration
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: Traffic congestion is one of the most pressing issues faced by people in urban areas today. Every day, countless individuals spend valuable time stuck in long traffic jams, contributing to frustration and inefficiency. Gridlock not only wastes time but also increases the risk of traffic accidents. Emergency services such as ambulances, fire trucks, and police cars are often delayed due to heavy traffic, making it harder for them to reach emergencies in time, which can result in tragic consequences. To address these challenges, we propose an innovative solution: an IoT-based automated traffic signal monitoring and control system. This system will allow for real-time management of traffic signals and offer manual override capabilities via the internet. By streamlining traffic flow and providing dedicated green corridors for emergency vehicles, this system will reduce congestion and potentially save lives by ensuring that help reaches critical situations more quickly.

articleTitle: LipWiz: A Proposed Approach towards Visual Speech Recognition
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: The act of lip reading, or visual speech recognition has attracted more researchers in the last few years as it can be employed in human computer interaction, enhancing accessibility and communication without sounds. This paper reviews different mechanisms that are designed for lip reading with respect to analysis of Lip-based Word Identification Zone (LipWiz) in the first place. In comparison with LipNet, some modifications are made in LipWiz, such as providing new datasets and replacing Bi-directional Gated Recurrent Units (GRUs) with Bi-directional Long Short-Term Memory networks for enhancing temporal sequence modelling. Moreover, LipWiz has been benchmarked with other recent lip reading architectures to show its improvements in accuracy, generalisation, and even computational performance. LipWiz exhibits far better accuracy, generalization, and performance in computation as compared to other architectures such as LipNet.

articleTitle: Predictive Model for Student Career Success Using Blockchain Technology and Machine learning
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: Using blockchain for student career prediction offers key benefits, including enhanced data security and privacy through encryption and immutability, ensuring personal information protection. It provides transparency and trust with a tamper-proof record of achievements and skills, fostering confidence among employers and educational institutions. Decentralization eliminates the need for a central authority, reducing risks of data loss or manipulation. Additionally, blockchain enables accurate traceability of student progress, ensuring accountability in career prediction data. Using machine learning to develop a prediction model for student career prediction offers substantial benefits by enabling personalized, data-driven insights that can significantly enhance career guidance. With this vast amount of data from various sources, identifying complex patterns and correlations that may not be evident through traditional analysis. This allows for highly accurate, individualized career recommendations, reducing biases and ensuring fair evaluations. Moreover, this model will continuously improve over time, adapting to new data and refining predictions, ultimately leading to more informed and effective career planning for students. Applying machine learning algorithms on student data stored on blockchain will provide exact information about students including their strengths and weaknesses both. This will lead to a better prediction and effecting planning.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Analysis of IoT and IoT Security Attacks: Understanding the Threat Landscape
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: IoT has remarkably changed the internet landscape since its introduction. Today, even an isolated physical device is provided with the internet, which allows it to exchange information with other devices. As much flexibility as these devices offer, they also have numerous security issues, causing threats to its users. Adversaries increasingly exploit the vulnerabilities in Internet of Things devices to execute attacks that can inflict significant harm on individuals, communities, and organizations. Consequently, prioritizing the detection, prevention and mitigation of the attacks is imperative to ensure safety and security. The paper provides an in-depth examination of internet of things (IoT) taxonomy, highlighting the associated challenges and security attacks within the IoT ecosystem, which subsequently gives insights into the vulnerabilities of the IoT ecosystem. Additionally, it includes a comparative analysis of various security attacks along with their impacts.

articleTitle: Analyzing the historical data and trends in Stock market using machine learning
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: The Stock Market is robust and huge as there is an involvement of multiple people in the process of buying and selling. The fundamental technical analysis of placing the order as Buy or Sell is very important. Many technical analyses are involved inside placing the right order. There are many tools and various studies done in the state of the art for predicting the market in a correct way. By the development of artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning, the research carried out in this work is to propose the efficient and suitable machine learning model which works with at most accuracy with the time series data. In connection with the same, the extension of Recurrent Neural Network as the Long Short Term Memory model is proposed and the results were observed. This work primarily focusses on improving the system by predicting the market close to the real and performing better with improved accuracy and technically worth competing with the existing methodologies

articleTitle: Performance Enhancement and Secrecy Analysis of Hybrid RF/FSO Communication Links Under Combined κ-μ Fading and Exponential Turbulence Conditions
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: In this study, the secrecy performance evaluation of hybrid RF/FSO communication systems over κ-μ fading and exponential turbulence channels are conducted. We analyse the secure information rate and evaluate the throughput and secrecy capacity of the system through simulations. The results indicate that the proposed hybrid system improves reliability and security by combining adaptive modulation, beamforming, and encryption to combat interference and secure data transmission. Geographical heat maps help to visualize the influence of environmental factors on system performance. Federated learning in hybrid RF/FSO systems have been investigated in detail through simulations and numerical results to show the considerable improvements in communication reliability and performance that the increased redundancy and robustness of the hybrid scheme provides. This helps gain valuable insights into a better design of wireless networks in the future by highlighting the benefits of hybrid communication techniques and simulation-driven design to enhance performance and security across diverse complex environments and conditions.

articleTitle: Decoding Cyber Fraud Schemes and the Rise of ‘Fraud-as-a-Service’
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: Dark web marketplaces have over time become the center of all illegitimate actions and a major challenge to law enforcement and cybersecurity professionals. This study will detail the dynamics within such platforms, with a narrow focus on prevalent cyber fraud schemes. Through digital ethnography and records analysis, merged data mining and forensic tools in studying 50 dark web marketplaces over 18 months. Our results have defined five main schemes, namely credential stuffing, RaaS, phishing kits, carding, and money mulling services. Organizational structures, cost models, and changes in tactics of each were subjected to systematic analysis. Observed the emergence of a 'fraud-as-a-service' model with relatively low barriers to entry for new entrants. The paper also draws attention to emerging gaps in modern cybersecurity practices and legislation that must form the basis of further work that should also bring in more active international cooperation, robust AI-based monitoring, and focused awareness campaigns. This study extends the existing knowledge of cybercriminal activities and provides practical policy recommendations for stakeholders, such as decision-makers, police authorities, or IT security professionals.

articleTitle: Robust Pre-Processing Strategies for Early Lung Cancer Diagnosis with Low-Dose CT Scans
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: Cancer that starts in the lungs due to the growth of abnormal cell in uncontrolled way is known as lung cancer. Tumors that prevent the lung from supplying blood with oxygen may develop because of it. So, it is important to detect it in its early stages. Low-Dose Computed Tomography (LDCT) scans play very important role to detect it in early stages. This work represents the various pre-processing techniques which are applied to the dataset of LDCT scan images to enhance the efficacy and accuracy of the system to detect Lung cancer. The several pre-processing techniques, including Gaussian Filter, TV (Total Variation) Method, Bilateral Method, Wavelet Method, Invariant Wavelet Method, NLM (Non-Local Means) Method and BM3D (Block-Matching & 3D filtering) Methods are used in this study. These methods are able to perform positive results for image enhancement, noise reduction, and feature extraction. The results of the study show that these pre-processing techniques not only improve the clarity of LDCT scan images but also enable more precise identification of suspected tumor locations. These pre-processing methods also improve specificity and sensitivity of the system. Through the ability to intervene earlier and increase the chances of patient survival, this discovery holds the potential to save lives. It also has a great deal of potential to advance the field of early lung cancer detection.

articleTitle: Multi-Channel Sales Forecasting in a Kenyan Retail Environment
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: The fast and continuous progress in technology is significantly impacting not only the dynamics of retail and e-commerce but also the innovations in sales forecasting. Identifying what could potentially be the most effective method available for predicting sales across online and offline sales channels in this rapidly growing market is becoming more and more crucial to business owners. This study on multi-channel retailing examines the performances of conventional time series forecasting models ARIMA/SARIMA and the more recent approaches like Facebook Prophet and RNN. For this purpose, Kenyan retail time series data of three years was utilized. Our findings highlight that among these methods, LSTM emerges as the top performer, demonstrating superior accuracy in capturing the complex characteristics of the sales data. It is also important to note that based on the results of the experiments, SARIMA still has potential especially in short-term predictions of time series with strong seasonality.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence Enabled Cognitive Computing for AlN/β-Ga2O3 HEMT
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: HEMT devices have potential to handle the fast processing in applications such as real-time diagnostics utilizing the artificial-intelligence (AI) enhanced abilities. Along-with this HEMT devices can be extensively used in radar and defense systems to obtain faster response time and threat detection. This integration of AI and cognitive computing enables pattern-recognition and adaptive learning. The cognitive computing techniques integrated with HEMT enables the real-time analysis and predictions. For precise sensor data the amplification should be done at either no or very less noise levels.

articleTitle: Intelligent Road Sign Detection and Categorization Framework
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: Research on an AI-enabled road sign detection system has been ongoing because of its numerous real-world uses. Many of the existing solutions, which frequently rely on numerous constraints, are still not reliable in practical settings. A reliable and effective road sign detection and classification system built on the cutting-edge YOLO object detector is presented in this study. Each detection stage involves training and fine-tuning the Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) to make them resilient to various situations, such as changes in the camera, backdrop, and lighting. We specifically designed a two-step method for object identification, using a basic YOLOV8 model to recognize road-sign symbols in real-time. In the second stage, we convert the model’s output into audio format. In one dataset, the resultant method produced remarkable outcomes. The dataset included 2093 frames from 20 distinct classes, and our system generated 59 frames per second (FPS) with a recognition rate of 94.9%. This was a significant improvement over the prior results (81.80%) and surpassed the commercial systems SqueezeNet and MobileNet (89.80% and 93.03%, respectively) as well as FasterRCNN. The commercial systems’ experimental versions achieved identification rates below 70% in our suggested dataset. However, with a precision of 97.4 and 35 FPS, our system outperformed.

articleTitle: Flood prediction near Yamuna express way a case study on Delhi
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: The area lies near Yamuna River in Delhi faces a frequent flood event, and with the increasing frequency and intensity of flood events highly impacted the human lives, infrastructure, and agriculture. Hence, there is a great need of accurate and timely flood prediction models. Traditional hydrological models are useful but often inaccurate for effective disaster management. The new technologies like machine learning are showing a prominent solution for the complex problems like flood. Therefore, this study conducts a comprehensive analysis of advanced ML(machine learning) techniques: Logistic Regression or named as LR, Support Vector Machines named as SVM, Random Forest named as (RF)and XG-Boost, in predicting floods in the area lies near Yamuna River by using GIS, Remote sensing data and seven flood influencing factors. The performance of the models is tested by using performance metrics such as accuracy, recall, Fl-score and precision. Further, the models were also validated using curve of AUC-ROC. The outputs reveal that XG-Boost out performs the other models in prediction accuracy. Logistic Regression and SVM also perform well, giving them viable options depending on the application scenario. This study examines the benefits and weaknesses of each model and recommends their use in flood-prone area near Yamuna River.

articleTitle: Enhancing DNA Sequence Analysis for Disease Diagnosis and Prediction Using Parallelised Hash-Based Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: DNA sequencing is a critical tool in genetics, helping to identify disease-causing mutations, predict disease risks, screen for genetic diseases, and monitor disease progression. By determining the order of nucleotides that make up DNA, DNA sequencing allows for the identification of genetic information in specific DNA fragments, entire genomes, or complex micro-biomes. It has transformed disease diagnosis and treatment and has applications in biotechnology, forensic science, and evolutionary biology. Comparing DNA sequences helps researchers identify genetic disorders, cancers, and antibody repertoires, leading to tailored treatments for individual patients. However, the diagnosis of diseases using DNA requires an efficient algorithm due to the large number of nucleotides in DNA sequences. The hash-based approach, an optimal string pattern-matching algorithm, is used to identify relevant patterns in DNA sequences. This approach has shown significant improvement in speed compared to the single pattern matching approach for finding multiple string patterns and a parallelized approach for hash based using GPU is also proposed.

articleTitle: Graph Based Automatic Text Summarization for Categorization of BBC News Articles
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: Large number of users use world wide web, news on news channels, weather reports, blogs, online available research works, online social media platforms and government reports, magazines to extract the useful information but due to enormous size of textual content in Petabytes or Zettabytes it is unfeasible to manually summaries the big data and extract the required information. Thus, the use of computerized text summarization is becoming more widespread. Research on text summarization has been conducted extensively in the field of natural language processing (NLP). There are numerous methods for automatic text summarization. Using the BBC News Summary dataset, this research employs a popular technique called graph-based extractive text summarization. It might be difficult to assess a text summary's quality; BLEU measurements and ROGUE variables are employed in this process.

articleTitle: Analyzing Impact of Data Augmentation Techniques in Computer Vision
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: Data Augmentation is a prevalent practice within computer vision, which uses transformations like random flipping, rotation, jittered colors and advanced techniques like Mixup and CutMix to artificially increase a training dataset. This, in turn, seeks to give generalization skills, minimize overfitting, and amplify the diversity of the data. In this paper, we explore the effectiveness of different data augmentation techniques for computer vision applications significantly concerning their effects on image classification tasks using convolutional neural networks (CNNs). The study bases its analysis on Residual Network-18 (ResNet-18), Visual Geometry Group-16 (VGG-16), Visual Geometry Group-19 (VGG-19), Densely Connected Networks-121 (DenseNet-121), and a Modified CNN. These were all trained and evaluated on the Canadian Institute for Advanced Research –10 (CIFAR-10) dataset. According to the results, the modified CNN model consistently attains the highest accuracy of the different tried models. Although its performance record of 90.9% with training augmented and 91.14% without augmentation is better than others, the results show an outstanding generalization capability of the model in different environments indicating resilience and adaptability of the model across an even wider variety.

articleTitle: Automating Talent Acquisition Assisted by Resume Parsing System for Enhanced Job Matching
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: Artificial intelligence has vast potential in resume parsing and human resource management. It aids in proliferating information and data sources, improving software's data management capabilities, and designing intricate and advanced algorithms. Al is changing the way firms hire and users interact with one another. This paper explores the development of a resume parsing system using the RoBERTa model to enhance job matching in talent acquisition. Traditional resume screening processes are time-consuming and prone to human error. Automated systems, although available, often require resumes to follow a specific format. This research presents a novel approach utilizing RoBERTa to parse resumes in various formats, thereby increasing the efficiency and accuracy of the talent acquisition process. The methodology includes the design and implementation of the system, followed by an evaluation of its performance. Results indicate significant improvements in processing time and matching accuracy. The implications of these findings suggest that organizations, regardless of size, can benefit from integrating such a system into their HR processes.

articleTitle: Evaluating Buffer-Based Optical Switch Architectures: Feedback vs. Re-Circulating Designs for Enhanced Network Performance
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: This paper presents a performance evaluation of optical switches utilizing feedback and re-circulating type buffer architectures, emphasizing their implications for next-generation optical networks. As data traffic continues to escalate due to advancements in digital applications, traditional electronic switching methods struggle to meet increasing demands for speed and capacity. Optical switches offer a compelling alternative by directly routing optical signals, thereby reducing latency and enhancing bandwidth. This paper presents the simulation analysis of feed backward and re-circulating type buffers in terms of throughput and scalability of both feedback and re-circulating buffer-based optical switches under varying traffic conditions. Simulation results confirm that while feedback buffers have low delay due to short storage duration while re-circulating switches demonstrate superior throughput capabilities during peak demand. The findings provide critical insights for network designers in selecting appropriate switching configurations to optimize performance in future optical networks.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Approaches to Assess Heart Attack Risk after COVID-19: A Comparative Study
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: The Corona Virus Disease of 2019, also known as COVID-19, spread like wildfire around the planet and the leading reason of mortality worldwide after COVID-19 is Heart attack. The SARSCoV-2 virus produced pandemic. It had enormous influence on global health, affecting millions of people worldwide. Physicians and researchers took note closely to the relationship between COVID19 and cardiovascular health. As the world enters the post-pandemic phase, long-term consequences of COVID-19 on heart conditions remain a concern. Heart attack cases are increasing. It is important to predict any such dangers. This study aims to evaluate different machine learning algorithms to anticipate risk of heart attack in patients after COVID-19. Fl-score, Precision and Recall are used for evaluating each model’s performance. Various Machine learning test models are used for it. The study focuses on people who suffered from virus and having a high chance of heart attacks in future. The purpose of this research is to analyze and predict the probability of cardiac arrest in Covid-19 patients using machine learning techniques. These algorithms are included in our dataset.

articleTitle: Evaluating Optimization Algorithms for Dynamic Workforce Management: A Comparative Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: Effective workforce management is critical for optimizing operational efficiency in dynamic environments, particularly in healthcare settings. This paper presents a comparative analysis of five prominent optimization algorithms—Genetic Algorithms (GA), Ant Colony Optimization (ACO), Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), Simulated Annealing (SA), and Tabu Search (TS)—specifically applied to the problem of dynamic staffing needs in hospitals. Each algorithm is evaluated based on key performance metrics, including execution time, solution quality, scalability, and robustness. The study reveals that while GA and SA deliver high-quality solutions, ACO and TS are better suited for dynamic environments where conditions frequently change. PSO is recognized for its speed but may compromise on solution quality in more complex scenarios. The findings suggest that healthcare practitioners should consider hybrid approaches that combine the strengths of these algorithms to enhance workforce optimization. Recommendations for future research include the exploration of adaptive algorithms and the integration of machine learning techniques to further improve staffing efficiency in healthcare and other industries.

articleTitle: Statistical Analysis of Social Media and E-commerce data to get insights on consumer behaviour
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: The universal influence of social media has become deeply ingrained in our daily lives, it has changed the mindset and behavior of the people. Customers' purchasing habits are also impacted by the rise in social media use since these platforms offer a wide range of products that go above and beyond what customers expect. As customers, we have begun to use it to research and purchase the goods and services that meet our needs. E-commerce platforms have allowed sellers to reach a wider audience and effectively market and sell their goods and services. These platforms also make it easier to gather important information and consumer input, which can be used to create marketing plans and regulations. This study aims to examine the impact of social media advertising on consumers' buying decisions across a range of demographic categories, such as age, gender, income, and education. Data has been analyzed and presented using a variety of statistical techniques, such as tabulation, pie charts, bar charts, and the Chi-square test. This study looks at the significant relationship between age and how social media marketing affects consumer buying decisions. The results of this study will help marketers prioritize these factors when creating marketing plans.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Analysis and Framework for Text and Graphics Separation in Document Images
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: The process of breaking up a digital image into many parts is called segmentation. These sections in scanned papers, are those that have backgrounds, texts, and images. In applications linked to document analysis, text segmentation is a significant issue. The separation of a complex document into non-text and text components is a major challenge in document image analysis. Localization of text in printed document images is a critical processing step for page layout analysis (PLA), specifically for obtaining textual data. Several algorithms have been developed for this subject. However, many algorithms only produce accurate answers for a limited type of documents due to their reliance on specific attributes or assumptions. There is a need to develop effective techniques for many sorts of documents, such as newspapers, magazines, documents, and articles, with arbitrary layouts and nonhomogeneous backgrounds. This study examines the various ways that distinguish between non-text and text in document images.

articleTitle: An Analysis of Various Classification Algorithms for Fake News Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: With the expansion of social media and advanced stages, the spread of fake news has ended up a noteworthy societal issue. This paper presents a comprehensive outline of machine learning strategies utilized for the detection of fake news. We talk about different approaches such as Natural Language Processing (NLP), unsupervised learning calculations, and machine learning models utilized within the recognizable proof of fake news. We dive into highlight designing, opinion investigation, and organize examination as key components of fake news detection frameworks. Moreover, we look at datasets, assessment measurements, and challenges related with detection of fake news. Through this analysis, we point to supply bits of knowledge into the current state-of-the-art techniques and headings for future investigate in combating fake news dispersal. This paper mainly used K-Nearest Neighbor, Jaccard similarity, LSTM, Decision Tree, and Logistic regression Classifiers for the classification. Main objective of this paper to verify the accuracy of models by performing the pre-processing the data and handle the imbalanced data more appropriately. The results of this papers show comparison of all classifiers with accuracy. Our results shows that KNN achieves 83%, 84% for Logistic Regression, 84% for Decision Tree, 85% for Jaccard Similarity & Random Forest is 85% and 98% for LSTM in our experiment.

articleTitle: Leveraging ResNet50 for Accurate Brain Tumor Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: Brain tumors are one of the foremost life-threatening diseases, producing serious complications that contribute to a heightened rate of morbidity and mortality. The emergence of deep learning strategies has vastly refined the process of identifying and categorizing brain tumors using MRI scans, providing crucial insights into the visualization of various structures within the human brain. Annually, countless individuals around the world receive a life-changing diagnosis of a brain tumor, and these cases often have low survival rates, underscoring the need for improved diagnostic approaches. This highlights the necessity for developing capable and systematic measures (improvement strategies) for diagnostics and treatment. While there has been progress in this regard, the search for a reliable detection system continues. In this paper, we focus on the ResNet50 model to enhance accuracy in detecting brain tumors. A type-curated ResNet50 is implemented for the brain tumor detection task, classifying MRI scans into two categories: 0 (Tumor) and 1 (No Tumor). Our findings reveal that the ResNet50 architecture successfully accomplished a classification accuracy of 97.3%, surpassing the VGG19 model, which attained an accuracy of 96%. This research seeks to contribute to the development of a robust and resilient model that enables healthcare professionals to make early and accurate decisions regarding brain tumors.

articleTitle: Advance Spam Detection Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: The rapid expansion of digital communication has resulted in a significant rise in unsolicited messages, commonly known as spam. This influx disrupts communication systems and consumes valuable resources. Although spam detection methods have advanced, ongoing challenges persist due to the constantly changing nature of spam and the unequal distribution of data, where legitimate (ham) messages far exceed spam in number. In this paper an optimize machine learning-based model is proposed for accurately classifying messages as either spam or ham. The model integrates the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) to handle data imbalance, ensuring more accurate and unbiased results to counteract dataset imbalance by creating synthetic samples of the minority class. This approach improves the model's ability to identify underrepresented spam messages effectively. The proposed model is more efficient and produces high accuracy of 98.38. Future research directions are also given to provide insights for researchers and security professionals.

articleTitle: Protecting Hearts with Support Vector Machine Analysis for the Early Detection of Heart Failure
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: In this research, the predictive modelling used is support vector machine (SVM) method that can easily handle a very high quotient of complex health data. Even though most of us lead stressful lives these days, it seems improbable that more people had really weak hearts in the past. Heart failure is when the heart is not really pumping along any more in its usual way. SVM is something that figures out who and when bad things might happen to you, which is to say, who really might have quite serious vascular issues. The remarkable 79% accuracy rate of the SVM’s classification abilities applies to a wide range of clinical indications and risk factors. This is pretty amazing. It now seems clear that if such predictions are used well, true doctors can radically change the way we think about healthcare by finding heart issues before they become big. And they can make healthcare cheaper in the process. This study is focusing a huge spotlight on how smart, informed computer methods are a must if we want to get truly good at finding and treating heart failure early—and on the road to much better ideas about keeping tabs on your health.

articleTitle: Decentralizing Cybersecurity: A Dynamic Distributed Honeypot System Leveraging Blockchain Technology
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: In the continuous expanding domain of cybersecurity, the rise of more cyber threats is also increasing. Therefore, it demands the development of more efficient defense strategies. In past, honeypots are used as lucrative devices to attract malicious activity. However, most of the honeypot systems are static in nature, which may not be efficient in distributed environment. This paper introduces a Dynamic Distributed Honeypot System (DDHS) for the same purpose. In these honeypots nodes are dynamically distributed and connected via blockchain technology, aimed at improving threat detection and response capabilities. By distributing honeypots across multiple nodes in a blockchain network, the proposed system is more secure against external attack. The paper defines the system's architecture, assesses Blockchain performance in terms of attack probability.

articleTitle: Generalized framework using Federated Learning for brain tumor detection from medical images
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: This paper presents federated learning to identify brain tumors based on MRI scans. A federated learning approach enables a model to be trained on decentralized data sources without requiring direct data exchange. In the field of medical imaging, where privacy rules restrict data exchange, this technique is very beneficial. The study investigates the categorization of brain tumors using EfficientNet, a convolutional neural network design. A federated learning configuration with twenty clients was designed to evaluate model performance. The results show that the federated learning approach using EfficientNet achieved an accuracy of 97.56% in detecting brain tumors. This research found that federated learning is valuable in brain tumor detection systems.

articleTitle: Exploring Machine Learning Algorithms for Early Diagnosis of Plant Disease
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: Plant leaf diseases threaten agricultural productivity and food security, affecting global crop production. Traditional detection methods are often time-consuming and error-prone. This paper explores using machine learning to automate plant leaf disease detection, improving speed and accuracy. Paper elaborates the execution of a comprehensive database of plant leaf diseases, detailing symptoms, environmental conditions, and affected species, to train. The experimental results generated through the implementation were tested with the state-of-the-art methodologies and found to be over 90% accurate. The proposed method outperformed the existing methods. The performance measures like the accuracy and other evaluation metric proved the efficiency of the methodology presented with improved accuracy. The outcome of the paper served as a socio-beneficial so as the reformation of agricultural practices have been emerged out. The new revolution in the modern agricultural practices had emerged owing to the inclusion of machine learning (ML) and the Deep Learning models in the early disease prediction in plant.

articleTitle: Leveraging RAG for Effective Prompt Engineering in Job Portals
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: Traditional recruitment methods are time-consuming and heavily reliant on manual processes, leading to inefficiencies. This paper explores the integration of AI technologies into a job portal to streamline the hiring process, focusing on AI’s ability to automatically parse and extract information from resumes and job descriptions to match candidates with relevant job opportunities. The platform leverages Large Language Models (LLMs) to extract key information, such as skills, education, and work experience, from both resumes and job descriptions. Fine-tuning through prompt engineering ensures accurate extraction, even when data fields are incomplete or missing. To further enhance matching accuracy, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) techniques are employed. These mechanisms retrieve relevant information from a structured skills database to provide context, which, combined with the generative capabilities of LLMs, enables more contextually accurate matches. Candidates receive personalized job recommendations based on the information extracted from their resumes, while employers can post job descriptions and use AI-driven tools to match candidates. This approach of using contextual prompts not only improves matching accuracy but also reduces computational time, eliminating the need for custom models tailored specifically to resumes or job descriptions.

articleTitle: Advancements in Image Synthesis with Progressive Generative Adversarial Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: An overview of the use of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) in computer vision—image synthesis and manipulation—is given in this study. A generator and a discriminator are two complex neural networks that are trained in competition to form GANs. Owing to the formidable capabilities of deep neural networks and their adversarial training approach, GANs exhibit the ability to generate realistic and plausible images, thereby demonstrating remarkable prowess across various applications in the realm of image synthesis and manipulation. This survey paper delves into recent GAN-related research. Working on the progressive GANs model technique, the authors find out how capable it is compared to other GANs algorithms. Building an image synthesis Progressive Generative Adversarial Networks (ProGANs) is a complex process with several steps that work together to produce high-quality pictures.

articleTitle: Towards Safer Communities: Real-Time Violence Detection and Instant Alerts using mobilenetv2
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: Violent actions represent a serious danger to public safety and the overall well-being of society. Traditional surveillance systems operate primarily reactively, necessitating the development of proactive solutions to detect and mitigate such incidents. It is imperative for monitoring systems to identify violent behavior in real time and promptly notify the authorities. Deep learning and computer vision have emerged as pivotal areas of research for advancing automated violence detection systems.This paper proposes a Real-Time Violence Detection and Alert System that employs the MobileNetV2 architecture to ensure effective and accurate classification of frames. The system integrates Cloud Firestore for secure and scalable data management, providing a database that authorities can utilize for analyzing and investigating future violence cases. Additionally, it employs a Telegram Bot for immediate incident alerts. With 96% accuracy, the system demonstrates reliability and adaptability across various environments, offering a robust and scalable solution for public safety while contributing to proactive crime prevention.

articleTitle: Cardiovascular Disease Prediction Using Machine Learning and XAI
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: Heart illness may be a critical wellbeing condition that includes an eminent effect on worldwide mortality, particularly among more seasoned people. Per WHO information, a stunning 17. 9 million people pass absent each year due to heart illness, showing a concerning increment within the number of cases. Distinguishing issues ahead of time through the application of machine learning strategies such as K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN), Random Forest, Decision Tree,Logistic Regression, Support Vector Machine, and Naive Bayes has the potential to upgrade determining accuracy and decrease the event of human botches. This think about evaluates different machine learning calculations on datasets that incorporate traits like age, sex, sort of chest torment, blood weight, and glucose levels. Through the utilization of Logistic Regression, a forecast precision of 83. 90% was accomplished. These improvements have the potential to progress the early location and treatment viability, eventually profiting pending healthcare strategies.

articleTitle: Enhanced Brain Tumor Detection via ResNet50 Classification and Residual U-Net Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: AI-driven dual-model system for brain tumor detection in MRI scans, combining classification and segmentation techniques. A ResNet50-based convolutional neural network (CNN) identifies the presence of tumors, while a ResUNet architecture ensures precise segmentation for accurate localization. To enhance localization, ResUNet architecture is employed for pixel-wise segmentation, providing precise tumour boundaries within the MRI images. By incorporating transfer learning techniques, the models benefit from pre-trained weights, significantly improving performance and reducing training time. Innovative use of Focal Tversky loss addresses data imbalance, improving segmentation accuracy for irregular tumour shapes. Experimental results demonstrate superior performance with 95% classification accuracy and a Dice score of 0.91 for segmentation. This dual-model pipeline offers a robust solution for early detection and precise localization of brain tumours, which is critical for timely medical intervention and improved patient outcomes.

articleTitle: Crime Pulse: Crime hot-spot detection using Machine Learning and Gen-AI*
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: The aim of this research is to determine the accuracy of machine learning algorithms in identifying high-crime regions. Traditional methods of locating crime hotspots, such manual analysis, are challenging and prone to errors. Machine learning offers a more accurate and effective approach. The study procedure includes preprocessing, determining pertinent characteristics, and collecting crime data. A range of machine learning algorithms that predict the likelihood of crime in different places will be trained using this data. The performance of these models will be evaluated using the pertinent metrics. The expected outcomes include demonstrating the value of machine learning in identifying crime hotspots, identifying suitable algorithms, gaining a better understanding of the factors that lead to hotspots, and developing a practical tool for law enforcement. The goal of this research is to make society safer and more secure by utilizing machine learning. Law enforcement organizations may more effectively deploy resources, discourage criminal activity, and eventually lower crime rates by accurately and efficiently identifying high-crime areas.

articleTitle: Graph Convolutional Neural Networks for Molecular Mechanism Exploration in COVID-19 Patient
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: This research aims to unravel the molecular subtleties of COVID-19 using Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs) for extensive protein profiling. The main objective is to decipher the intricate relationship between viral and human host proteins to have a better grasp of disease path physiology and possible treatment options. The goal of this study is to use GCNs to identify structural motifs, functional pathways, and critical protein-protein interactions that are involved in viral infection and the control of the host immune response. The study's overarching goal is to aid in the creation of better diagnostic instruments, therapeutic approaches, and vaccinations against COVID-19 by clarifying these molecular pathways. In addition, by using multi-omics data, this study aims to improve GCNs' predictive power in defining new protein interactions and finding druggable targets. This study aims to speed up the identification of much-needed antiviral medicines by using cutting-edge computational approaches to shed light on the path physiology of COVID-19. The long-term objective is to address the continuing worldwide health catastrophe caused by the COVID-19 pandemic by creating a collaborative platform for multidisciplinary research that brings together computational biologists and experimental virologists. Using a variety of criteria, the Kaggle database shows (i) how two cities lived during COVID-19, (i) Bike_ID, Rental_ID, Duration in hours (min 60, max 1380), Start_Station ID, which can be anything from one day to three or four days in the future, with a unique range of values from 0.0927542 to -0.197574, Latitude from 51.506 to 51.4996, and (iii) Transactions done during COVID-19 with a range of values from 1494460 to 232629023, with a class type of 1,2, or unknown, and a duration in hours (min 60, max 1380).

articleTitle: Addressing Research Gaps in Object Detection: A Model for Infrared-Based Low-Light Conditions
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: Object detection is the backbone of many modern real-world applications, including autonomous driving, surveillance, and robotics. As the object detection technology improves, particularly convolutional neural networks (CNN), the accuracy of such systems has improved drastically. Each of object have their own set unique characteristics which are used for purpose of object classification which is the backbone of object detection. Despite advancements there a few research gaps such as struggle to detect small and/or partially hidden objects, domain adaptation, multi-object tracking, unbalanced data, etc. Multiple approaches are used for object detection such as R-CNN, speedy R-CNN, Faster R-CNN, and YOLO to name a few. Finally, a model is proposed for object detection in low light conditions using near infrared imaging trained using YOLOv8 which can detect classes like vehicles and persons. The study resulted in maximum F1 score of 0.81 and mAP of 0.924.

articleTitle: Enhancing Security and Transparency in Video Conferencing Systems through Blockchain Integration
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: Even though virtual meetings are in use as the key communication source, there exists a greater requirement now that the privacy of these telemeetings needs to be assured and guaranteed. This paper therefore presents a novel approach towards boosting video conferencing systems’ security and transparency concerns in the adoption of the blockchain technology. It would utilize blockchain’s decentralized ledger for proper and safely secured meeting data using tamper-proof and transparent controls with access. Since smart contracts can actually automate rules governing access, thus reducing reliance on central authorities, it also mitigates the risks of unauthorized entry, data breaches, and inherent security failures. The immutable nature of blockchain ensures that all access control data is safely recorded and cannot be changed: this is very important for the integrity of the data as well as for supporting auditability in general. For instance, this can ensure regulatory compliance by providing a robust and transparent audit trail. Our solution also answered key challenges such as scalability and user experience by adding a streamlined interface, thus making it accessible and efficient for a wide range of users. With these innovations, this paper provides a whole-rounded blockchain-driven platform that empowers people with enhanced security, privacy, and trust for any safer and more efficient virtual collaboration in today’s digital landscape.

articleTitle: Optimized Mutual Authentication and AES Encryption Framework for Enhanced Security in Multi-Server Environments
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: This paper introduces a secure authentication framework by applying Mutual Authentication Coupled with Optimised AES (Advanced Encryption Standard) Encryption to improve the security of the multi-server environment. By addressing inefficiencies in traditional mutual authentication protocols without encryption, this framework significantly improves both performance and resilience. Encryption time was reduced by 25% and authentication time by 16.67% while CPU (Central Processing Unit) usage was reduced by 23.08%, with a corresponding 21.43% improvement in memory efficiency. The proposed system demonstrates a 70% improvement in attack resistance. Dynamic revocation mechanisms mitigate unauthorized access and malicious activity in real time. The protocol is designed for resource-constrained environments to ensure secure, scalable, and efficient communication in multi-server architectures, further increasing system reliability and user trust in cloud-based services.

articleTitle: Hybrid Machine Learning for Feature-Based Spam Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: Researchers have been paying significant attention to the increasing need for and prevalence of unwanted spam on networks. Multiple studies have extensively examined the fundamental origins of spam in networks. Previous research has shown that spam-related problems are one of the main dangers to network systems, affecting both ongoing operations and past data. To tackle and reduce the increase in spam, researchers have put forward different methodologies. Although certain techniques have received approval from experts, every method has its own set of constraints. Furthermore, the persistent issue of inadequate precision in identifying spam poses a significant obstacle for numerous current predictive models. Therefore, the task of finding a reliable prediction method continues to be a challenging and extensively studied field, attracting significant attention from researchers in recent decades. This paper introduces a machine learning approach for detecting spam in emails. The proposed model demonstrates improved accuracy compared to previous studies.

articleTitle: Exploring the determinants of AI driven FinTech adoption by Indian farmers for sustainable agrarian economic development
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: This paper explores the transformative potential of AI-enabled FinTech in agriculture, an area relatively understudied compared to other industries that have benefited from such innovations. The study investigates important factors such as Social Influence (SI), Performance Expectancy (PE), Convenience (C), and Price Value (PV) and their significant impact on farmers' intention to adopt FinTech solutions. Empirical evidence is provided through the application of Structural Equation Modelling (SEM) using PLS4 on survey data from 266 farmers. The findings indicate that SI, PE, C, and PV strongly influence farmers' technology adoption, emphasizing the need for social interaction and knowledge sharing, especially in semi-urban and rural communities where social media is less prevalent. The study recommends that FinTech companies should enhance their offerings through interactive features, training, and educational programs, particularly around social gatherings, while governments should promote FinTech adoption by providing support services like lower loan interest rates and comprehensive education initiatives. The research highlights psychological and experiential factors as more critical than physical dimensions, positioning agriculture as a competitive sector. It also addresses the need to study technology adoption across different demographics, underscoring the importance of localized, rather than universal, FinTech strategies. Overall, this research advances knowledge on AI-driven FinTech adoption in rural economies, providing a basis for interdisciplinary collaboration and future technological advancements in agriculture.

articleTitle: Fuzzy Logic and Fog Computing in Electronic Health Records Data Privacy: A Comprehensive Review
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: The potential to improve healthcare services has drawn attention to the use of fuzzy logic and fog computing into electronic health records (EHRs). This study offers a thorough analysis of the research on Fog Computing (FC) enabled Fuzzy Logic c-based EHR systems. While fog computing allows for real-time data processing and decentralized storage near end users, fuzzy logic provides a reliable method for handling ambiguities in patient data, diagnoses, and decision-making. When combined, these technologies enhance data security, scalability, and system responsiveness. This research paper includes major approaches, architectures and important applications such as in cloud computing fog-based solutions reduces bandwidth and latency related issues with the help of fuzzy logic how clinical decision support system improves. In this study we list the future research possibilities to address these type problems and also explains obstacles such as complexity of computing, interoperability and privacy of data. These type of study assists academics and practitioners to creating effective, intelligent and safe EHRs’ system. In this research paper privacy preservation of EHRs addressed by integration of fuzzy logic with fog computing.

articleTitle: Securing Software Defined Networks from Packet Injection Attacks: A Framework for Detection and Prevention
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: Software Defined Networking (SDN) has changed how networks are managed by splitting the control and data layers, allowing for centralized control and flexible network setups. SDN increases programmability, flexibility, and agility but also presents serious security risks, especially with regard to packet injection attacks. These attacks specifically target the central SDN controller, which serves as a single point of failure, by taking advantage of security flaws in the SDN architecture. Attackers can send unauthorized packets into the network, causing communication issues, damaging data accuracy, and thereby leads to Denial-of-Service (DoS) attack. This paper examines the threat landscape of packet injection attack in SDN environments, with a focus on the OpenFlow protocol, which serves as a communication bridge between the control and data planes. We explore how attackers create fake hosts to get around traditional security defences. The research also provides a novel and efficient solution to cater this attack. The solution is compared with the existing state-of-the art solutions to ensure its accuracy and efficiency. We show, by direct observation, how these methods strengthen SDN security against packet injection attacks, improve network reliability, and provide a safe and dependable network environment.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Artificial Intelligence Approaches in Deceptive Opinion Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: The deceptive opinion spam directly threatens the integrity of online review platforms, which in turn erodes consumer trust and fair competition. In this study, we explore and compare the performance of traditional machine learning models such as Logistic Regression (LR), Support Vector Machine (SVM) as well as recently released advanced deep learning models (BiLSTM, BERT, XLNet, T5, Capsule Networks) to detect deceptive reviews. The research tests different feature representations (unigrams, bigrams, trigrams, TF-IDF) as baseline augmented performance metrics using datasets such as Deceptive Opinion Spam Corpus. The XLNet led all models with the highest performance at 89.69% accuracy and 90.03% F1 score, emerging as the most effective on aggregate. The BERT T5 models provided high precision, BiLSTM served the purpose with balanced performance, and Capsule Networks demonstrated its promise in capturing hierarchical relationship structures in text data. As a result, this study contributes to opinion spam detection by suggesting good solutions and open tracks for future refinements, such as hybrid model development or domain-specific fine-tuning.

articleTitle: Health-Bot: AI-Driven Textual Question Answering for Medical Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: In the contemporary healthcare landscape, the imperative to deliver accessible, efficient, and affordable services is increasingly critical. A Chabot/dialogue system is a computer program which holds a conversation via auditory or textual ways. Such programs are specifically designed to provide the user a clone of how a human will chat and thereby it acts as a conversational partner. In this paper, we move beyond the notion of conventional Chabots towards developing a dialogue system for automatic medical diagnosis that converses with patients to collect additional symptoms beyond their self-reports and automatically makes a diagnosis. This research paper introduces Med-Bot, an advanced conversational Chabot designed to transform patient interaction and preliminary diagnosis through the use of Natural Language Processing (NLP). Med-Bot leverages a comprehensive medical knowledge graph and decision tree algorithms to effectively predict diseases based on symptom analysis. Initially, when a user reports symptoms, Med-Bot performs a targeted symptom analysis to ascertain the primary health concerns. It then utilizes probability analysis to dynamically generate follow-up questions, refining the context and precision of the user’s health status. The decision tree model, central to Med-Bot’s predictive capabilities, processes these inputs to identify and suggest potential diagnoses. This paper demonstrates how Med-Bot significantly reduces healthcare costs and enhances service accessibility, making it a pivotal development in digital healthcare tools.

articleTitle: Transparent AI Solutions for Parkinson’s Disease Diagnosis and Monitoring: A Multimodal Deep Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: Parkinson’s disease (PD) diagnosis remains challenging due to the variability in motor and non-motor symptoms. While deep learning (DL) models show promise in improving diagnostic accuracy, their "black box" nature limits clinical adoption. This study proposes an explainable AI (XAI) framework combining DL models with interpretability techniques, such as SHAP and LIME, to enhance transparency and trust. Using multimodal datasets, including clinical, imaging, and wearable sensor data, the framework identifies key features driving predictions, enabling clinicians to make informed decisions. The proposed method achieves superior performance, with an accuracy of 92%, precision of 91.1%, and recall of 90.4%, outperforming existing methods. By bridging the gap between AI outputs and clinical needs, this framework offers a practical tool for early PD diagnosis and progression monitoring.

articleTitle: Explainable-ML-based Framework to Predict Software Defects in Real-Time Control Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: Machine Learning (ML) algorithms have significantly improved software engineering activities by examining software metrics and repositories, leading to more accurate predictions and improved software quality. Here, we have used five Machine learning models, which are Random Forest, Bootstrap aggregating, Extreme Gradient Boosting algorithm and K-Nearest Neighbours algorithm, to compare which performs the best in software fault prediction, specifically targeting real-time control systems where reliability and responsiveness are critical. Comparing the results of the model we infer that the boosting algorithm has the highest accuracy, while still maintaining other evaluation scores. After thorough evaluation we got the maximum accuracy of 0.78 with the bagging algorithm. We have also added a layer of transparency by using X-AI. For this, we have used Shapley Additive Explanation (SHAP) and Local Interpretable Model (LIME). The results from both techniques support each other, and the feature which has the maximum impact is the number of lines of code. X-AI enhances predictability by unveiling the black box and revealing what features have the most impact on classification, which is especially important in ensuring the stability and safety of real-time control systems.

articleTitle: Leveraging Graph Neural Networks for Improved Fraud Detection in Financial Transactions
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: Fraud detection has been pressing with the elevating rate of fraud activities in financial transactions. Traditional methods often fail to identify complex patterns within large-scale data. The paper reviews Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) and their applications for enhancing fraud detection by graphical modeling of financial transactions, which creates an environment for capturing intricate connections among entities. We provide a GNN-based framework experiment with a comprehensive dataset, representing accuracy with better precision against traditional models. In this paper, we will present some solutions to overcome the challenges when deploying real-world GNNs into the banking system and open up the potential for GNNs to become one of the critical tools in the prevention of unauthorizedtransactions for financial institutions. Also, we will be discussing libraries such as NumPy, Pandas, Seaborn, Matplotlib, Warnings, Scikit- Learn etc. for carefully visualizing data and for carefully analyzing the performance of our model. For choosing a powerful methodology, the exhibition of different calculations is looked at, for example, Logistic Regression, Decision Tree Classifier, Random Forest Classifier, Support Vector Machine (SVM), K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), and Gradient Boosting Classifier for distinguishing bogus exchanges. Further, we will also be displaying numerous analysis of fraud indicators, anomalies, and transaction data which helps in deeply understanding transaction behaviors.

articleTitle: VisionAid Band: Real-Time Smart Navigational and Alert Support System for Visually Impaired Persons Using Wearable Technology
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: The "VisionAid Band" represents a groundbreaking advancement in assistive technology, designed to empower visually impaired individuals by enhancing their spatial awareness and mobility through an innovative, low-cost solution. Utilising an Arduino-UNO, ultrasonic sensor, and vibrator sensors to interpret the environment, translating physical obstacles into auditory or tactile feedback that guides users safely around their surroundings. The device’s affordability and simplicity are pivotal in addressing the accessibility gap in current assistive technologies, which are often prohibitively expensive or complex. This paper details the development process of the VisionAid Band, from conceptualisation to prototype testing. It discusses the selection of the microcontroller platform, sensor integration, and the development of algorithms that efficiently process sensor data to provide real-time, intuitive feedback to the user. Emphasis is placed on the device’s design considerations, including ergonomics, power consumption, and user interface, ensuring that the VisionAid Band is effective but also comfortable and user-friendly. Through a series of controlled experiments and user feedback sessions, the effectiveness of the VisionAid Band in improving navigational abilities among visually impaired participants is evaluated. Preliminary results indicate a significant enhancement in users’ ability to navigate complex environments safely and confidently. The paper concludes with a discussion of potential improvements, future enhancements, and the broader implications of the VisionAid Band on the accessibility and independence of individuals with visual impairments. The VisionAid Band exemplifies how low-cost, technology-driven solutions can substantially impact the quality of life for people with disabilities. Its development underscores the potential of innovative engineering to address critical challenges in accessibility, paving the way for more inclusive technology solutions in the future.

articleTitle: Secure and Optimized Cloud Storage with Privacy Preservation using Improved SHA-256
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: With the increased reliance of enterprises on cloud storage solutions for data management, maintaining safe and efficient storage while emphasizing privacy protection is crucial. With an emphasis on user privacy, this study examines the methods, tools, and difficulties currently involved in attaining safe and effective cloud storage. It looks at access control protocols, encryption techniques like SHA-256, and new technologies that are intended to improve the security and effectiveness of cloud storage systems. The study also addresses the changing trends influencing the security of cloud storage in the future and emphasizes the significance of adhering to privacy laws.

articleTitle: Transforming the Prognosis of Chronic Illnesses: Using Machine and Ensemble Learning to Provide Precision Healthcare
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: Chronic disease represent a global health concern that impacts families, individuals, and healthcare systems. The "Smart Healthcare" era's introduction of cutting-edge technologies has created new opportunities for the management and prognosis of chronic illnesses. The use of ensemble learning approaches to predict long-term health outcomes for common disorders such hepatic carcinoma, cataracts, colorectal cancer, gastrointestinal neoplasms, pulmonary cancer, and cardio- cerebrovascular diseases is investigated in this work. The study assesses how well ensemble learning models predict the course of chronic diseases using a variety of datasets. The Google Collaborator platform was used to carry out the experiments in a controlled, simulated setting. The results highlight how these prediction models can improve healthcare tactics by offering actionable insights, enabling more effective interventions and decision-making.

articleTitle: Integrating Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning for Folklore Preservation and Innovation
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: In an age where traditional cultures are dealing with the weight of globalization, there is folklore as the means of history, morals and ethics, and societal identity. A diverse oral culture of India that embraces myths, legends, customs and rituals has always been transferred from generation to generation regardless of technological presence. Since the concept of modern technology, particularly Artificial Intelligence and ML have come into the limelight, which provides newer dimensions for keeping up and transforming these rich Indian cultures and traditions. The role of AI and ML is preserving and safeguarding Indian folklore by transcribing, cataloging, indexing and analyzing massive collections of vocal cultures. However, AI-based tools like SVM, Random Forest, Decision Tress, Natural Language Processing are considered for their prospective to preserve and protect threatened Indian dialects, as well as AI-based storytelling platforms have initiated creative, vibrant and lively folklore versions. The incorporation of AI in cultural conservation brings several ethical concerns, from probable cultural misrepresentation to the likelihood of homogenizing varied narratives. At the end, this study emphasizes that, if applied with precision, AI can help as a safeguard and as nurturer of folklore, and therefore supports its continuity and significance in a swiftly changing world.

articleTitle: Review on Predicting the Landslide Susceptibility using Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: This Landslide susceptibility prediction is a critical task for Alleviating the risks associated with landslide hazards, which have significant socio-economic and environmental impacts. Existing techniques face challenges related to data quality, model coherence, and generalizability across diverse geographical and climatic regions. Additionally, while advanced machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) models offer high accuracy, they often require significant computational resources, which limits their practical application in real-time scenarios. In this review, we aim to highlight the strengths, limitations, and potential improvements of machine learning techniques in predicting landslide susceptibility, providing a comprehensive reference for researchers and practitioners in this domain. Furthermore, the role of Explainable AI is examined to address the critical need for interpretable and transparent models in real-world applications. Hybrid ML-DL models outperform traditional methods in handling complex spatial-temporal data, with dynamic factors improving accuracy and reliability. Explainable AI enhances interpretability, while advancements and collaborations address data and generalizability challenges.

articleTitle: Neural Network, Random Forest Classifier and Monte Carlo Sampling Based Binding Affinity and Pharmacological Analysis of Natural Analogues of Raf-1 Kinase Inhibitor for Breast Cancer Therapeutics
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: Raf-1 kinase activity in the MAPK/ERK signalling pathway has been linked to increased proliferation in breast cancer. The existing drugs have shown limited therapeutic efficacy. Thus, the study aimed to identify ligands targeting Raf-1 through artificial intelligence approaches, coupled with Monte-Carlo sampling docking algorithms. The study reviews existing sampling algorithms, along with the application of neural network and random forest classifier-based algorithms with under-the-hood molecular docking. A systematic database search for natural analogues of Sorafenib, the leading Raf-1 drug, was carried out from ZINC (>37 billion compounds) and SuperNatural 3.0 (445000 compounds). NNScore 2.0 (neural network), and DeepChem (random forest classifier) predicted binding scores of natural ligands against Raf1 Kinase Protein. Glide (in Schrodinger Suite 2023-1) which runs on Monte Carlo sampling, was used for molecular docking. MMGBSA analysis (OPLS_2005 force field and PRIME VSGB 2.0 solvation model) predicted free binding energies of ligand- Raf-1 complexes. Pharmacological (ADME/Tox) properties of the ligands were predicted to evaluate their safety profile. The natural ligand, ZINC000002148905 (binding energy= -56.66 kcal/mol), stood as the best natural analogue among the top four ligands from all the programs. In this artificial intelligence- driven pharmacoinformatic analysis, the natural analogues were modelled for further in vitro experimental analysis to inhibit Raf-1 and pave the way for natural therapeutic options for the treatment of breast cancer.

articleTitle: The Role of the Metaverse in Advancing Cybersecurity Practices and Threat Mitigation
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: Metaverse technologies are growing rapidly and come with unprecedented cybersecurity challenges that cut beyond any traditional digital context. Researchers have thoroughly researched virtual worlds and their cybersecurity, but the metaverse’s ongoing digital identities, integrated economies, and immersive social interactions have prompted a need to rethink and reformulate current security paradigms. How can the metaverse become a testing field as well as an implementation platform for advanced cybersecurity practices? To analyze metaverse-based security simulations, we applied a mixed-methods approach that involved quantitative analysis of 2,500 simulated attack scenarios and qualitative assessment of 150 expert interviews in 12 countries. Findings show that metaverse security simulations outperform traditional testing environments by up to 47% in terms of threat detection rate, especially when detecting complex, multi-vector attacks.
