The study also found that immersion visualization of network threats in the metaverse showed a notable improvement in incident response times (34%) and team collaboration in security operations centers. Therefore, summarizing our conclusion, the metaverse uniquely provides advantageous opportunities for training in cybersecurity, threat visualization, and real-time response coordination while introducing new vectors of attacks with innovative protection strategies. Such results have far-reaching implications regarding the future of cybersecurity training and operational security management in increasingly immersive digital environments.

articleTitle: Towards Designing an Information Superhighway for Neurological Disorders
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: Neurological Disorders impact a subject’s/ person’s nervous system in various ways and include a wide range of neurological conditions. More often than not, the impact is life altering and affects the subject’s communication skills, social interaction capability, etc. If the condition is detected at an early age, it can significantly enhance the quality of life of the subject with focused training, treatment, etc. Detection through brain scans, behavioral analysis, etc. are costly and time consuming. Recently artificial intelligence (AI) models are being increasingly used for detection & classification of neurological disorders based on various parameters and datasets. However, for an end user, it’s still very difficult to realize the power of these models end to end viz., from data acquisition to generating recommendations. Hence, in this paper, we present the architecture of an Information Superhighway in the form of AI pipeline. The task of the Information Superhighway is to enable capturing the multimodal data (image, video, etc.) of a subject from a smartphone of a laptop webcam, and send this through a secure information channel to a cloud storage. On the storage, the data is managed using various Big Data technologies and is acted upon by the DL models. The generated recommendations are sent back through a different secure communication channel back to the mobile or laptop. We feel that our work is first of its kind which makes the technology transfer possible for the end user and utilize full the prowess of powerful AI models.

articleTitle: AI-Powered Transcript Summarization and Question Answering for YouTube and Wikipedia
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: With the rapid growth of online content, there is an increasing demand for efficient tools that facilitate content understanding and knowledge retention. This research focuses on the development of an AI-powered system designed to automate summarization, question answering, and quiz generation from YouTube transcripts and Wikipedia articles. The system employs advanced natural language processing (NLP) techniques to process and distill complex information into clear and concise summaries. The process begins with the extraction of text through the YouTube Transcript API or web scraping. The Pegasus-XSum model is then used for summarizing the content, ensuring that key information is retained while minimizing text length. For question answering, the Llama model is employed to generate contextually relevant answers based on the provided content. Additionally, the system generates quizzes by extracting entities from the text to enhance interactive learning. This technology aims to improve content comprehension, making it especially valuable for educational settings and knowledge management. By integrating summarization, question answering, and quiz generation into a single platform, the system supports efficient learning and better retention of critical information. This research demonstrates the potential of NLP in addressing the challenges of information overload and facilitating effective knowledge acquisition.

articleTitle: AI-Driven Software Reuse: Optimization and Comparative Performance Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: Software reuse improves productivity and ensures that there is less time delivered to the market by enabling the proper usage of reusable code from the software repositories. The study provides the collaboration between the AI techniques, which includes Convolution Neural Networks (CNN), Random Forest (RF), and Support Vector Machines (SVM), to predict software components' reusability. The comparative analysis shows the effectiveness of different AI- driven algorithms, where CNN has shown the highest accuracy of 92%, thus reducing the human effort in finding the reusable modules. The Case studies in e-commerce and health care show the benefit of using AI-driven reuse of software; this means that the development time is reduced by 25%, and the maintenance cost is decreased by 20%. The paper highlights how different AI algorithm integration with software engineering has some limitations. The findings show that AI has greatly revolutionized software reuse. Thus bringing innovation and efficiency in software engineering.

articleTitle: Travel Itinerary Generation using AI and Recommendation Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: The rapid growth of artificial intelligence (AI) in the travel and tourism sector has revolutionized the way how tourists plans their trips. Personalized travel suggestions are provided by AI-powered systems, which streamlines the usually laborious process of organizing trips. This paper examines the integration of machine learning, natural language processing, and recommendation systems with a focus on AI-based travel itinerary generators. These programs can provide personalized itineraries by analyzing user preferences, including time, money, and hobbies. To improve personalization, methods including sentiment analysis (Logistic Regression), content and collaborative filtering, and K-Means clustering are used. Based on user’s input, Point of Interests (POIs) are filtered and ranked. Time slots are assigned within the itinerary and ordered to minimize travel time using K-means clustering algorithm. A hybrid of collaborative and content filtering is applied based on user feedback on which sentiment analysis is performed using logistic regression. The final itinerary is generated that includes suggested POIs with suggested start and end times. This paper illustrates how current developments in AI-driven travel solutions might improve user contentment and simplify travel arrangements. Notwithstanding these developments, issues like data privacy and personalization biases still need to be addressed in order to guide future studies.

articleTitle: Revolutionizing Forensic Odontology with Artificial Intelligence: A Systematic Review
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: Forensic odontology is the branch of dentistry that deals with the proper collection, handling, and presentation of dental evidence to the court of law. It requires the expertise of a forensic odontologist. It can be time-consuming and strenuous in case of mass disasters. This has led many professionals to use automation. AI is revolutionizing healthcare; it is changing the practice of medicine (including dentistry), science, and policy. Dentistry and forensic odontology have been utilizing advances in diagnosis and treatment planning through the use of various AI-driven software and applications. AI applications in forensic science promise notable gains in efficiency and accuracy, particularly for disaster victim identification. The use of artificial intelligence (AI) in forensic odontology is discussed in this article along with the most recent findings and suggestions on ongoing translational advancements in intelligence.

articleTitle: A Data-Driven Approach for Elderly Activity Recognition: Using Wearable Sensors and AI Models
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: As the elderly population rises in healthcare centers, monitoring their daily performance makes it difficult to identify miracle signs of an anomaly or an emergency. Activity recognition systems (ARS) to enable elderly care have become necessary because such persons require independence with consideration of their safety. Nonetheless, there is some discomfort in implementing HAR, such as sensor accuracy, a variation in health among seniors, and cognitive diversity. This paper focuses on the analysis of HAR systems for recognizing the behavior of the elderly through smartphone sensors, including accelerometers and gyroscopes. To enhance the studies of data classification, machine learning classifiers such as k-Nearest Neighbors (k-NN) and Random Forest were utilized to increase the overall accuracy. Linear regression was also employed to analyze sensor information and individualize observation. The accuracy of the chosen models indicates that the Random Forest model is best to predict the training results288. The abilities shown by these models included handling data unpredictably and featuring important information that was deemed valid. Furthermore, a possible incorporation of HAR systems with smart grid (SG) monitoring is discussed as an extension of the work for elderly care in smart homes. The feasibility of the proposed system was further demonstrated using evaluation criteria of accuracy, precision, and recall. Based on the findings of this research, we can recognize that integrating AI-driven HAR models with SG technologies might enhance elderly monitoring, creating a more innovative, accurate, and individual approach to senior care. This research provides a foundation from which to improve the living standards of elderly people, allowing them to live their remaining years safely and as independently as possible.

articleTitle: Deepfake Detection using XAI based Deep Fusion Models
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: Deepfake technology has rapidly evolved, posing a serious threat to the authenticity of digital media and contributing to the spread of misinformation. The manipulation of media content raises significant concerns across sectors like politics, entertainment, and social media, undermining public trust in digital information. In response, this research proposes an advanced deepfake detection model that integrates Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) techniques within a hybrid deep learning architecture. The proposed model combines ResNet50 and Vision Transformer (ViT) to capture spatial and contextual features effectively. While exploring additional methods such as facial landmark detection and frequency domain analysis, the final model focuses on the ResNet50-ViT combination for its superior performance to fusion model. To ensure transparency, the model employs XAI techniques such as LIME (Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations) and SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations), offering interpretability by revealing the key factors that influence its predictions. This dual focus on high detection accuracy and interpretability ensures that the model not only detects deepfakes effectively but also builds trust in automated decision-making processes. By leveraging cutting-edge deep learning and XAI methods, this framework offers a more reliable, transparent, and adaptable solution for preserving digital media authenticity across various applications, ultimately contributing to combating misinformation and fostering trust in digital content.

articleTitle: Advances in Fuzzy Relation Inequalities and Optimization Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: Fuzzy relation inequalities (FRIs) play a crucial role in various optimization and decision-making problems that involve uncertainty and imprecision. The solution of such inequalities has been an active area of research, leading to the development of a wide array of advanced algorithms designed to handle fuzzy constraints in optimization problems. This paper reviews the most prominent algorithms developed for solving fuzzy relation inequalities, focusing on the evolution of methods from traditional linear programming to modern metaheuristic algorithms. We explore linear programming approaches that integrate fuzzy relational constraints using different composition operations, such as max-min, max-Łukasiewicz, and addition-min compositions. The advancements in these methods, particularly in handling large-scale and complex fuzzy systems, are highlighted. Additionally, the paper examines the application of metaheuristics, including Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), in solving fuzzy optimization problems under relational inequalities. The use of bipolar fuzzy relations in optimization models is also reviewed, emphasizing their ability to model conflicting objectives in decision-making. Moreover, geometric programming, hybrid algorithms combining fuzzy relations with other optimization paradigms, and future trends in integrating machine learning techniques into fuzzy optimization are discussed. The review provides valuable insights into the state-of-the-art algorithms for fuzzy relation inequalities, offering potential directions for future research and applications in dynamic, real-world systems. The proposed methods are crucial for improving decision-making in fields such as healthcare, finance, and intelligent systems, where uncertainty and imprecision are inherent.

articleTitle: Predictive Analytics in AI Marketing: Transforming Consumer Engagement
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: The accelerated use of artificial intelligence in digital marketing, the possibilities of engaging with the consumer through providing individualized experiences have grown immensely. This research investigates the role of predictive factors in the enhancement of social media marketing strategies through a dataset that includes 300,000 campaigns spread out on Instagram, Facebook and Pinterest. The methods Ethical Considerations in the analysis include logistic regression, T-tests and ANOVA, which were used to analyze variations in conversion rates, back end audience targeting and the factors affecting success of the campaigns. The results indicate that advertising on Instagram for the younger demographic groups is also more effective than other forms of advertising because of the platform’s focus on engagement. However, challenges such as privacy concerns, biased algorithms, and legal compliance issues persist. Case studies of Amazon, Starbucks and Netflix show how collaborative filtering along with AI-based personalization methods increase user satisfaction and retention. The findings underscore the evil of customer abuse for coming up with marketing strategies and the role of ethical AI in sustainable advancement of marketing in digital space.

articleTitle: An Effective Agricultural Produce Object Detection System: YOLOv5-Based Classification
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: Automated object detection (OD) in real-time agricultural applications poses unique challenges due to uneven lighting conditions, object similarities, and cluttered environments. In comparison to standard object detection tasks, agricultural OD requires models that are both efficient and lightweight, enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices. This study introduces a novel agricultural produce detection system based on the YOLOv5 architecture, specifically designed to classify "Green Chilli," "Red Chilli," and "Eggplant." The YOLOv5 model was customized to handle these specific crops and optimized for deployment on edge devices by converting the model to TensorFlow Lite (TFLite).To enhance detection accuracy, advanced techniques such as data augmentation and hyperparameter tuning were applied. The TFLite model was optimized to run efficiently on IoT devices and low-powered CPUs, same as the Jetson Nano and Raspberry Pi, ensuring smooth real-time inference without the need for cloud-based computation. The SIoU loss function was utilized for precise localization, especially in densely packed images. The proposed system demonstrates high accuracy, precision, and recall, achieving a mAP) of 96% on a proprietary dataset of 600 images. The system's lightweight nature and real-time detection capabilities make it an effective tool for automating produce sorting and quality assessment in agricultural and food processing industries.

articleTitle: NEMO: ML based fish species classification
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: This paper describes the creation of an ML-based tool for image-based identification of fish species commonly found in Indian oceans, addressing the issues that fishermen experience in accurately reporting their catch. Motivated by the Smart India Hackathon (SIH) issue statement from the Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services (INCOIS), our goal is to improve marine fishing advice services. We developed a dataset that includes photos of 21 fish species typically captured by Indian fishermen, precisely chosen to ensure clarity and little background noise. Using this dataset, we applied transfer learning to eight different pre-trained models to determine the most effective one for deployment in a mobile application. The Kotlin-developed program has an easy-to-use interface with catch history, fish nutritional values, and pertinent weather data. Our findings show that the installed models can correctly recognize fish species, with MobileNetV2 reaching a peak accuracy of 97.61%. In addition to expediting the species identification process, this cutting-edge tool provides fishermen with crucial information, which eventually leads to more accurate species-level catch reporting.

articleTitle: Optimised Data Encryption and Search Efficiency Framework Using Memory Modules for IoT Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: The proliferation of IoT devices necessitates secure and efficient mechanisms for data encryption and retrieval. This paper presents an optimized framework that leverages AES encryption integrated with memory modules to enhance security and operational efficiency. The proposed system introduces a dynamic key generation mechanism to mitigate key reuse vulnerabilities and incorporates a memory module to achieve reductions in encryption and search execution times by 80% and 79%, respectively, compared to traditional methods. The framework also ensures secure cloud storage of encrypted data and supports privacy-preserving retrieval using trapdoor functions. A Java-based implementation validates the system's scalability, robustness, and platform independence for real-world IoT applications. By addressing key challenges such as data integrity, confidentiality, and low-latency operations, the proposed framework offers a comprehensive solution tailored to the evolving needs of the IoT ecosystem.

articleTitle: Bridging Healthcare Gaps: Sustainable Liver Disease Diagnosis Using Machine Learning in Resource-Limited Regions
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: Liver disease is a major global health issue, and proper diagnosis at the right time is crucial for treatment. This paper discusses machine learning methodologies in the detection and diagnosis of liver diseases such as hepatitis, cirrhosis, and hepatocellular carcinoma. It addresses the diagnostic complexities such as nuances in liver function tests and variability in symptoms and explores how ML can leverage diverse data sources, including medical imaging, genetic markers, and clinical data, to improve precision and efficiency. The study applied advanced Python tools and algorithms with 10-fold cross-validation for splitting the dataset. Random Forest had the highest accuracy at 99%, followed by SVM and Gaussian Naïve Bayes. The research will provide an affordable diagnostic tool, especially for developing countries with a high burden of liver disease, which will contribute to SDGs 3, 1, 10, and 9 through improved access to healthcare, reduction of economic burdens, and innovation. The future directions are multimodal data integration and personalized diagnostic systems for further improving the outcomes in patients.

articleTitle: Prediction Of Student Dropout Analysis For Education using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: In previous years the quantity of understudy dropout from the instructive organization is expanding quickly. The high pace of understudy's dropout in an enlisted course has been a significant danger to numerous instructive establishments or colleges. The understudy enters the establishment with bunches of dreams and assumptions. At the point when their assumptions are not satisfying or certain elements like socio economics will impact and makes them drop from their enlisted program. It is a significant danger to all instructive organization. The different procedure of the dimensionality decreases, which incorporates highlight determination and component extraction. Include choice is bit by bit strategy that is utilized to choose the right trait from a given property sets. For the component extraction process, it includes the change of higher aspects' information in comparing lower aspects. Include choice comprises of elements like Scholastics, demographical factors, mental variables, medical problems, instructor's perspective, understudy conduct. In this paper, we acquaint a strategy with foresee the understudy dropout involving Guileless Bayes Grouping Calculation in R language. And furthermore, inspect the justification for understudy drop out at an early state and foresee regardless of whether the understudy will drop. There are many elements that influence an understudy to commit dropout as we referenced previously. Early dropout expectation assists the association with holding the understudies from the particular scholastic program.

articleTitle: Improving Traffic Sign Recognition with the YOLOv9 Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: Modern intelligent transportation systems and autonomous driving technologies are quite helpful in light of the population's increasing growth, and they work particularly well when used in conjunction with traffic sign monitoring. By giving drivers accurate and exact traffic signals, such as speed limits, warnings, and directional assistance, this makes transportation much safer. Autonomous vehicles must correctly understand these indicators in order to make wise driving judgments. Accurately identifying and classifying a wide variety of traffic signs in a range of environmental circumstances is a difficulty. A cutting-edge deep learning model created specifically for object recognition tasks is called YOLOv9 (You Only Look Once version 9). In addition to offering respectable speed and accuracy, YOLOv9 expands on the advantages of its predecessors by implementing cutting-edge strategies such as PGI and GELAN. Because of these improvements, YOLOv9 is especially ideal for real-time applications like recognition of traffic signs, where more accuracy and quick and accurate object identification are essential. With an increased accuracy the results demonstrate the model's stability and dependability and show that it is appropriate for real-world uses in autonomous driving and traffic control. Subsequent investigations will concentrate on improving resilience in various situations, utilizing semi-supervised learning, creating more resource-efficient models, broadening the range of datasets, and combining traffic sign recognition with additional autonomous driving tasks. The development of dependable and effective traffic sign detection systems is furthered by this work.

articleTitle: Unified Framework for Outlier Detection Using Ensemble-Based Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: In this study, we propose a unified approach to anomaly detection that integrates density-based fuzzy clustering with ensemble learning to improve detection accuracy and efficiency. The framework utilizes multi-layer perceptron (MLP), support vector machine (SVM), and k-nearest neighbors (KNN) classifiers, leveraging their complementary strengths for robust anomaly detection. To ensure comprehensive evaluation, the model is validated on multiple datasets, including NSL-KDD and CICIDS 2017, demonstrating its generalizability across diverse environments. Optimization strategies, such as bootstrap aggregation, are incorporated to address computational overhead while preserving performance. Furthermore, metrics like Jaccard, Dice, and Kappa are employed to provide detailed insights into model performance, ensuring interpretative clarity. By integrating federated learning for privacy preservation and explainable Al techniques for transparency, this work addresses critical challenges in anomaly detection. The results obtained as Sensitivity 92.48%, Specificity 99.73%, Accuracy 99.53%, Precision 97.96% and Recall 92.48% highlight the model’s ability to deliver high accuracy, efficient computation, and equitable performance, making it a significant contribution to the field.

articleTitle: Assessing ChatGPT’s Influence on Productivity and Learning Outcomes in Higher Education: A Comprehensive Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: This paper investigates the influence of ChatGPT on efficiency and learning within higher education, demonstrating its significant role in enhancing progress towards achievement of Sustainable Development Goal 4(quality education). A study conducted by researchers at a leading university in Northen India surveyed over 431 students and faculty members. Data was analyzed using statistical analysis and revealed how ChatGPT impacts the learning and hence the overall productivity of students. High engagement was observed, with correlations between increased usage and enhanced perceived support for learning (r = 0.45) and productivity (r = 0.55). Productivity analysis revealed significant differences across usage frequency groups (F- Statistic = 272.46, p-value ≈ 0). Personalized learning experiences provided by LLMs are helping students to skill up and Faculty to prepare the students to enter the workforce with a proactive learning mindset, aligning educational outcomes with industry needs.

articleTitle: Next-Generation IoT Intrusion Detection: Leveraging Hybrid Deep Learning Algorithms for Enhanced Security
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: Wireless sensor node and DDoS (Distributed Denial of Service) is a major attack way that can exhaust the energy of a sensor, disrupt the communication traffic of an IoT network. We must be on the lookout for these attacks. With the quantity of sensor nodes, traditional methods face difficulty in detecting network traffic analysis requiring big data analysis. This paper is dedicated to Network Traffic analysis using Big Data environment and detecting attacks using Deep Learning. Implemented with PySpark in Google Colab, using Keras and Scikit-Learn built-in libraries. To be more specific, training and testing are conducted on the ’CICIoT2023’ / ’TON IoT’ datasets, respectively. When we use a correlation feature reducer, it virtually considers the most significant features for inclusion and reduces all of our features. The first contains a hybrid deep leaning model combining one-dimensional EfficientDet and Gradient Boosting Machine (GBM), comparing it with ten other algorithms. It generated 99.95% binary classification accuracy for the CICIoT2023 dataset and 99.75% for TON IoT data.

articleTitle: AI-Driven Evolution in HR: A Bibliometric Study on Professional Roles and Skill Adaptation
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: This bibliometric analysis examines the impacts of artificial intelligence (AI) and automation on roles and competencies in human resources (HR), identifying key themes and collaborative patterns in the field. A search conducted in Scopus on October 7, 2024, using “artificial AND intelligence AND automation AND human AND resource AND roles OR skills” initially retrieved 218 documents. Non-English and pre-2015 articles were removed, resulting in a final sample of 208 documents. Core trends and connections between prominent authors, institutions, and countries were mapped through co-authorship, keyword co-occurrence, and citation analyses using VOSviewer software. Findings reveal an international focus on skill adaptation, digital transformation, and AI-augmented HR competencies, highlighting an evolving collaborative effort to address automation challenges. This study enhances bibliometric literature, paving the way for future HR research in the AI era.

articleTitle: Message Priority Classification Framework for Autonomous Vehicles in Supply Chain Management
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: In modern supply chain management, efficient communication and timely decision-making are essential to ensuring smooth operations and avoiding descriptions. This is ensured by efficient communication and timely decision-making. Prioritizing essential messages with these systems becomes essential as autonomous technologies become more integrated. This work presents a message priority classification framework formulated to refine communication processes within autonomous vehicles (AVs). This plays a growing role in supply chain logistics. Our framework uses machine learning (ML) models such as Support Vector Machines (SVM), K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Random Forest (RF), and Logistic Regression (LR) which are implemented to classify message priorities in real-time, assuring efficient and uninterrupted communication. The experimental outcomes show that the RF model outperformed other models and achieved the highest accuracy of 0.9714. Further, the proposed framework enhances the modularity of AV communication systems and supports efficiency in decision making in complex and variable supply chains. This study emphasizes the significance of ML in optimizing communication leading to more dependable and efficient supply chain operations for AVs.

articleTitle: Universal System for Higher Accreditations (USHA): Novel Blockchain-Based Educational Transcripts Issuance and Verification Architecture
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: Blockchain technology (BCT) offers a concrete solution to combat the transcript counterfeit by shifting trust from human oversight to immutable encrypted data on a decentralized network. Despite the prevalent usage of existing blockchain-based systems in many institutions, some unresolved concerns persist due to technical challenges and data protection laws like the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR). This research explores the existing blockchain-based transcript (BCBT) frameworks and proposes a novel architecture named Universal System for Higher Accreditations (USHA), combined with Interplanetary File System (IPFS) and issuance of soulbound tokens (SBTs). The present study outlines the fundamental concepts of blockchain and their relevance to BCBT, inheriting IPFS for the encryption and decentralized storage of records, resulting in file size compression of over 99% in comparison to existing digital transcripts maximum size. In addition to this, the use of SBTs ensures transcripts are paired to identities that can’t be transferred or revoked by the owner, absent in NFTs. The study makes a comparative analysis to highlight the need for blockchain-based over digital and paper- based transcripts in the modern digital world. The present study proposes a novel architecture framework, USHA, and stakeholders (students, university, verifier) roles and responsibilities based on the related study of architecture in existing use of universities since 2016-2024 and two related studies—NFTCert and RejSBT. Moreover, the paper compares the USHA architecture with NBF Lite powered by Vishvasya Blockchain Stack, a blockchain framework following Indian government legal compliances to issue certificates. Further, the paper states the applications of the USHA architecture, extending further to the technical, legal, and regulatory challenges involved, and concludes the study with future research opportunities.

articleTitle: Resource Allocation in IoT Networks via DQN and PPO Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: Since the last couple of years has witnessed a steadily increasing demand for IoT-based services, their corresponding cloud infrastructures must distribute and allocate resources in efficient and dynamic manners. Workloads from the Internet of Things devices are diverse as well as changeable, so traditional resource allocation strategies are not suitable. In this work, the problem of dynamic resource allocation in cloud environments for datasets on the Internet of Things is explored and applied with RL techniques, such as DQN and PPO. The dynamic state of cloud resources, such as CPU, memory, and bandwidth usage, is introduced. By considering resource allocation as a Markov Decision Process (MDP), an investigation was made regarding how the RL algorithm can optimize the use of resources while adhering to SLAs. DQN value-based reinforcement learning technique is used to evaluate the best allocation rules by estimating Q-values of state-action pairs. On the other hand, PPO is a policy-gradient method used to optimize the policy directly and provide stability and robustness in continuous action spaces. In this evaluation, an Internet of Things-based dataset was used to evaluate both algorithms regarding dynamic modification of allocation resources few SLA breaches, and improved resource utilization efficiency. A comparative result shows that PPO does a better job compared to DQN in scaling any kind of resource continuously with higher rewards and faster convergence compared to the former approach. This work demonstrates the potential for RL-based techniques for cloud resource management within the Internet of Things ecosystems.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Based Model to Recommend Safe Route Navigation System
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: The level of crime rates in practically every part of the world has risen to unprecedented levels. These are tough times that call for extreme methods to protect individuals, particularly those who must travel to unknown and known locations on a daily basis. Regardless of the mode of transportation used by the victim walking, driving one's own car, using a public transportation vehicle, autorickshaws, or taxis the majority of these crimes happen when the victim is traveling. This research suggests a Deep Learning Based Model To Recommend Safe Route Navigation System that shows the user a safe path shown on maps and based on the area's historical criminal history. Our approach is implemented in a hierarchical manner: a Decision Network is used to determine the user-specific attributes in the first place, and then that same Decision Network is used to activate the creation of safe routes via Geospatial Data Analysis. Users can view the navigated routes of the effective system as a colour coded map. Acknowledging that the real consequences which our research strive for should produce, we validated our model with specific data of San Francisco city for demonstrative purposes.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Based Phishing Website Detection System - Natural Language Processing Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: Natural language processing (NLP) methods can be used to identify phishing websites in addition to static and dynamic features. Phishing sites frequently include certain phrases, misspellings, or misleading text patterns in their material, as well as other visual cues and language that match those of authentic websites. Through the examination of textual components such anchor texts, meta-descriptions, and homepage titles. The proposed model is able to comprehend the linguistic traits that are frequently seen in phishing websites using NLP-based features like sentiment analysis, keyword matching, and phrase frequency to increase model's sensitivity. In addition, we use real-time URL parsing to detect possible dangers as users come across them, guaranteeing prompt notifications and lowering the possibility that phishing attempts would be successful. Our study emphasizes how crucial it is to keep improving and upgrading phishing detection models because attackers usually change their strategies.

articleTitle: A Unified Object Detection Framework for Front Vehicle Behavior Prediction using YOLOv5s and Ontology Reasoning
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: In autonomous driving and advanced driver-assistance systems (ADAS), safety and efficiency rely heavily on accurately forecasting front vehicle behavior. This study presents a unified object detection framework that combines ontology-based reasoning with YOLOv5s, a compact and high-performance object recognition model, to improve the prediction of front vehicle behavior. The YOLOv5s model ensures real-time detection of vehicles and traffic objects while providing crucial spatial and contextual information. Complementing this, ontological reasoning leverages domain knowledge—such as traffic laws, vehicle interactions, and environmental factors—to infer high-level behavioral patterns, including lane changes, braking, and turning. By integrating ontological reasoning with the speed and precision of YOLOv5s, the proposed system effectively analyzes vehicle behaviors and predicts potential hazards. Evaluations on real-world driving datasets demonstrate that this unified approach significantly enhances behavior prediction accuracy compared to standalone detection methods. This fusion of machine learning and symbolic reasoning enables autonomous driving algorithms to make more reliable and anticipatory decisions, contributing to safer and more efficient driving systems.

articleTitle: An Analysis of Deep Learning Algorithms for Detection of Pulmonary Illness
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: The necessity for highly precise and rapid methods of diagnosis is highlighted by the important role that pulmonary illnesses make to the global health burden. Enhancing diagnostic accuracy and speeding up detection through the use of algorithms that use deep learning presents a substantial opportunity for better patient outcomes and more efficient healthcare procedures. In proposed article, the authors provide the special technique for recognizing pulmonary illnesses from medical imaging data by using deep learning algorithms. We offer a thorough method that integrates CNNs with additional deep learning methods to diagnose diseases with high accuracy. Through a detailed literature review, we highlight the existing research in this domain and identify gaps and challenges. We discuss the methodology, techniques employed, challenges encountered, and potential future directions. The author’s findings show how well the suggested method works to identify pulmonary diseases, finding the exact path for enhanced diagnostic systems in healthcare. Our study demonstrates algorithms in pulmonary disease detection, outperforming traditional methods, ensuring robustness across diverse datasets, and offering clinical utility with interpretability insights.

Author Keywords: Diagnostic Methods for Pulmonary Diseases Disease detection

articleTitle: Data-Driven Approaches to Weather Prediction With Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: Weather forecasting joins among the most critical undertakings in agriculture, disaster management, transportation, and many other sectors. Though traditional forecasting techniques are commonly employed, they tend not to model the non-linear behavior of the atmospheric systems correctly. Thus, this study aims at improving the accuracy and efficiency of weather prediction through machine learning techniques. Considering a dataset composed of daily meteorology descriptive variables such as average temperature, humidity, wind speed, etc. and a barometric pressure, the research analyzes the effectiveness of the following machine learning algorithms as Linear Regression, Random Forest, Decision Tree and Support Vector Machine. Preprocessing of the data set included missing value treatment, feature enhancement and time-series modelling. Also, temporal analysis included season, trends and other variations which are time dependent. Models were further assessed by performance indices such as the Area Under the Curve, F1 Score and Accuracy. Results obtained suggest that complex weather patterns are best captured using more complex models such as neural networks and ensemble methods in comparison to simple models. As this study shows, machine learning may assist in improving the weather forecast by making it more accurate and more efficient. In addition, such use of these models can enhance the management of weather-sensitive sectors. The next steps will include the use of actual data collected in real-time and taking into consideration deep learning models to increase the prediction accuracy and scale, and also the ability to do multistep forecasting.

articleTitle: Efficient Intrusion Detection and Trust Management in Federated Learning Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel Multi-Stage Anomaly Detection System (MSADS) to combat Fake Traffic Injection (FTI) attacks in federated learning (FL). The MSADS incorporates data normalization and statistical thresholding to establish baseline performance profiles for model updates. Anomaly detection is enhanced through the use of clustering algorithms, which group data points based on similarities. Local Outlier Factor (LOF) assessments further identify deviations that may suggest malicious activity. Additionally, a Reputation-Based Trust Framework (RBTF) is developed, assigning dynamic reputation scores to clients based on their update quality, thus fostering accountability and peer review mechanisms. Finally, Federated Defense Mechanisms (FDM) leverage the decentralized structure of FL to implement strategies like model diversity, homomorphic encryption, and decentralized aggregation, reducing the risks associated with FTI. By integrating these methods, the proposed approach strengthens the security of FL systems while ensuring robust model performance and privacy. This research highlights the critical need for proactive measures in securing federated learning against sophisticated threats, ensuring a collaborative environment where clients are motivated to contribute authentically. The findings emphasize the importance of adaptive security protocols in the evolving landscape of distributed machine learning.

articleTitle: Behavior-Based Machine Learning Approaches for Malware Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: The present research investigates the implementation of various methods of machine learning to analyze fluid information from executable files for the purpose identify contamination. We extracted feature vectors from a dataset that contained both malicious and benign samples. Standard metrics like F1-score, recall, and precision were used to train and evaluate a range of classifiers, including Decision Trees, Random Forests, Support Vector Machines, and Logistic Regression. Our test findings show that the models successfully distinguish between harmful and benign files, with Random Forest providing the highest level of consistency in all evaluation measures. These Results demonstrate the promise of machine learning methods to improve systems for detecting malware.

articleTitle: Enhancing Weather Prediction Accuracy with Gradient Boosting: A Machine Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: This research focuses on the integration of Machine Learning (ML) in predicting the climate with the help of daily recorded weather dataset of Seattle [33] which we obtained from the Kaggle. This research focuses on implementing and analyzing multiple ML techniques such as Naive Bayes, K-Nearest Neighbors (K-NN), Support Vector Machine (SVM), Gradient Boosting, XGBoost, and Decision Tree. XGBoost able to get to the top position with an accuracy rate of 87.90% which speaks volume of its performance. This integration of ML techniques is useful in understanding the weather prediction which is highly complex due to multiple atmospheric changes. Such modern methods help in recognizing the more complex non-linear features and trends within weather data. Machine learning algorithms makes it possible to detect such tendencies from complex datasets over time. ML enhances weather prediction approaches by learning and analyzing patterns from historical data and real time data. This paper highlights the importance of extreme gradient boosting in weather forecasting by providing examples of its successful applications within the interdisciplinary field of meteorology and ML. This study compares different algorithms for best accuracy and also points to the increasing significance of ML in the enhancement of weather forecast models.

articleTitle: Ethereum’s Merge: A Comprehensive Analysis of Per-Block Energy Consumption, Greenhouse Gas Emissions and Block Size
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: This paper presents a comparative analysis of Ethereum’s pre- and post-Merge performance, focusing upon energy consumption, GHG emissions, and scalability due to increase in block size. These findings contribute to understand the potential to change in consensus mechanism of blockchain technology for future years aligning with global sustainable development goals. This research analyses per-block energy consumption, size and greenhouse gas emissions (GHG) before and after the Ethereum’s Merge event (September 2022). During the Proof of Work (PoW) age (2015-2022), Ethereum’s energy consumption surged from 0.01 TWh to 17.4 TWh, highlighting the environmental impact that inspired the transition. The transition from PoW to Proof of Stake (PoS) consensus mechanism noted the energy reduction of over 99.9%, with the energy consumption of 13.98 GWh and carbon dioxide emissions at 1.7 kilotons in 2024, estimated by Cambridge Bitcoin Electricity Consumption Index (CBECI). Post-Merge block size analysis reveals a significant change in the block size over the period of years with cumulatively average block size expansion of 16,000% from 2015 to 2024.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis of Different Machine Learning Techniques Used in Software Effort Estimation
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: Software effort estimation is a vital component of project management, encompassing the prediction of time, cost, and resources necessary for software development. Accurate effort estimation plays a pivotal role in effective project planning, resource management, and budgeting within the realm of software engineering. However, software effort estimation is challenging due to project complexity, evolving requirements, and the unique nature of each development environment. In recent years, various machine learning techniques, including regression, fuzzy logic, support vector machines, decision trees, genetic algorithms, artificial neural networks, ensemble methods, clustering, K-nearest neighbors, logistic regression, random forests, and hybrid approaches—have been employed to improve estimation accuracy.This research delivers a comparative evaluation of these machine learning methods, considering performance metrics such as mean absolute error, accuracy, root mean square error, mean relative error, usability, and scalability. Special attention is given to ensemble methods, which often outperform individual models in accuracy. The findings offer guidance for researchers and practitioners in selecting optimal machine learning techniques for software effort estimation, ultimately enhancing tool development and modeling accuracy for sustainable software development.

articleTitle: Evaluating Generative Models: A Review of Challenges and Opportunities in Assessment of Generative Adversarial Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: Generative adversarial networks (GANs) have achieved remarkable success in image synthesis but evaluating their quality remains an open challenge. Existing automated metrics like FID are unable to fully capture generation performance across both objective fidelity and subjective aesthetic attributes important to human perception. This paper conducts an extensive review of literature on GAN evaluation methodology. Key limitations of current approaches are analyzed through a discussion of popular metrics and their inability to predict human judgment comprehensively. To address this, a novel hybrid evaluation model is proposed that combines automated scores with human ratings to provide a more balanced assessment. A pilot study demonstrates the hybrid metric can predict human response more accurately. However, additional validation is required. The review emphasizes the need for evaluation systems integrating richer human input to better optimize models according to user priorities. Interactive frameworks and techniques from computational creativity may help advance assessment towards comprehensively benchmarking generative capacity and artistic exploration.

articleTitle: Facial Emotion Recognition From real-time videos using CNN Model
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: Facial expressions are an exciting study area within Computer apparition, affecting estimating, and human-calculating interaction. Our approach offers a distinct end-to- end network for attention-based self-governing face emotion recognition. The new network design’s four components are modules for feature extraction, attentiveness, and categorization and reconstruction. Through the extraction of textural information from the image and the detection of minute changes in facial expressions, Network performance can be enhanced by the properties of the Local Binary Pattern. Through a mechanism for attention, the neural network may be trained to rank critical components first. The neural network may be trained to prioritize important elements using an attention mechanism. CNNs in feature extraction and pattern recognition, we aim to classify facial emotions such as joy, sorrow, rage, shock, fear, and contempt in situations that happen in real-time—expression datasets, such as FER2013 and CK+. The experimental findings confirm the feasibility and efficacy of the recommended strategy.

articleTitle: Fall Detection and Alerts in Hearing Aids for Deaf using Generative AI
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: Individuals with sensorineural hearing loss often experience difficulty comprehending speech when background noise is present. This paper investigates the extent of this problem in various listening scenarios and with different types of background sounds. Additionally, the section explores the contributing factors to this challenge such as reduced audibility, reduced frequency selectivity, loudness recruitment, and dead regions in the cochlea where there are no surviving inner hair cells and or neurons. The sections evaluate different techniques for compensating for the effects of these factors. While signal-processing methods using the output of a single microphone to compensate for reduced frequency selectivity have had limited success, techniques utilizing multiple microphones have proven effective. Amplitude compression has also been effective in compensating for the effects of loudness recruitment, enabling individuals to understand speech across a wide range of sound levels. Next, the paper delves into the technical aspects of implementing fall detection systems in hearing aids. learning algorithms are also investigated for their potential in enhancing fall detection accuracy and minimizing false alarms. Furthermore, the importance of user-friendly interfaces and customization features in ensuring the effectiveness and acceptance of fall detection alerts is also highlighted. The paper also addresses the ethical and privacy considerations associated with fall detection in hearing aids. It emphasizes the need for transparent data handling practices and user consent, while also addressing potential concerns related to user autonomy and intrusion.

articleTitle: Architectural Trade-off Analysis of Modern Service Mesh Designs: A Qualitative ATAM Study
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: Modern cloud native applications are highly dependent on service mesh designs, which provide solutions for communication, security, and observability. Architectural decisions for service mesh implementations involve numerous trade-offs that affect system quality. This study analyzes three popular service mesh architectures: Istio, Linkerd, and Consul Connect, using the Architecture Tradeoff Analysis Method (ATAM), we created a utility tree that considers essential quality attributes such as security, maintenance, reliability, and operability. Our analysis identifies important areas of sensitivity where architectural changes have a significant impact on quality attributes, as well as trade-off points where increasing one attribute affects others. Our research identifies common trends in how service mesh designs handle opposing requirements, including proxy deployment, control plane distribution, and configuration management approaches. Our analysis shows that, while all systems prioritize security and observability, they differ dramatically in how they handle the complexity-flexibility trade-off. This analysis offers a systematic approach for software architects to evaluate service mesh designs and understand their trade-offs, leading to better architectural decisions in microservices environments.

articleTitle: Smart Plant Irrigation System with Arduino Uno and Soil Moisture Sensor
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: Automatic Smart Plant Watering System is a smarter solution that works on Arduino Uno, which can automatically operate for plant watering at optimal moisture conditions of soil. It checks the moisture with the help of a soil moisture sensor and, once the level of moisture goes down below a threshold, initiates a water pump. This user-friendly system is also energy efficient, making it suitable for busy or travel users, further contributing to sustainability plant care, thereby making it ideal for residential and nursery settings while emphasizing the promising use of smart agriculture and IoT technologies. This paper focuses on developing a smart water framework designed to efficiently manage water distribution based on real-time soil and environmental conditions.

articleTitle: Analyzing Sentiments in Twitter Data on Russia-Ukraine Conflict Using Machine Learning Methods
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: As the conflict between Russia and Ukraine has deepened and more international countries have been engaged, it has become critical to ascertain if the universal message is one of support for or opposition to military activities. This goal is supported by research on how public opinion and foreign affairs are critically connected. As a result, researchers looked at how the global community felt about Russia's invasion of Ukraine. In total, 27,894 tweets with the hashtag #UkraineRussia that were published on the first day were examined. The findings indicate that some of the most often recurring words in the tweets were "war," "people," "world," and "people." Sadness was the most prominent emotion, and negative sentiments were higher than positive sentiments. It was discovered that nearly 89% of conflicts involved the word "world" when a term was supervised in context concordance analysis. This finding underlines the rising worry that the situation between Russia and Ukraine may worsen

articleTitle: Harnessing Piezoelectric Energy for Smart Streetlights and Wastebin Automation
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: In this article, a new way to power streetlights and waste bins without using regular electricity is presented. This system uses a special material called piezoelectric that can turn the mechanical energy from people walking or cars driving by into electricity. This electricity charges a battery, which then powers the lights and sensors. These sensors help in the management of the lights and the waste bins in a more effective and practical way. It is clear that technology works towards achieving a more stable economy, and the same goes for this solution as it lowers the dependence on fossil fuels and pushes toward greener solutions. In simple terms, using the energy from people’s movements to power important parts of city infrastructure, like streetlights and waste bins. This system shows that advances in technology can really make a positive difference for the future.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Insights into the Influence of Business Incubators on Startup Success
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: The paper emphasises the effect of incubator services on startup success indicators such as revenue growth and survival rates. This paper creates a prediction framework that links crucial incubation services to startup success outcomes using machine learning models. This study qualitative in nature. The results show how important incubator services are for improving startup performance. To forecast startup results based on the availability of particular incubation services, a machine learning-powered recommendation engine was developed. Policymakers and incubator managers might use the findings to customise support services for a bigger impact. By filling in gap or literature in this domain about the direct correlation between incubation services and company success, the study adds to the body of literature on entrepreneurship and provides a data-driven approach to optimizing business incubators.

articleTitle: Developing an AI-Based Library Assistant: Enhancing Book Retrieval with Natural Language Processing and Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: The current college library system is hindered by inefficiencies in book searching, availability updates, identity verification, and checkout processes, resulting in delays and errors that negatively impact student experiences. This research paper presents an AI-based librarian system designed to address these challenges through automation and digital transformation. Leveraging a Large Language Model (LLM), the proposed system facilitates personalized interactions between students and library resources. Upon student verification, the AI librarian provides real-time information on book availability, location, and tailored recommendations, significantly reducing the time spent on manual searches. The streamlined checkout process allows for automated book issuance and instant confirmation notifications, minimizing human error and enhancing record- keeping. This innovative solution not only improves operational efficiency but also enriches the user experience by offering a user-friendly interface and timely assistance. Future enhancements, such as voice integration and mobile application support, are suggested to further modernize library services. This research underscores the potential of AI technologies to revolutionize library management and improve service delivery in academic settings.

articleTitle: Performance Comparison of Deep Learning Models in Predicting Stock Prices
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: The stock market in India is highly volatile, dynamic, and nonlinear, presenting significant challenges for researchers in time series forecasting. Predicting stock prices accurately has remained a critical topic of interest for both financial analysts and technical researchers. In this study, we deploy four deep learning models—LSTM, GRU, Simple RNN, and CNN1D—to predict the one-day-ahead closing prices of 20 prominent Indian companies grouped into five sectors: Communication Services, Consumer Cyclical, Energy, Healthcare, and Technology. The models were evaluated using five metrics: Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE), Normalized RMSE (NRMSE), and Coefficient of Determination (R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>). Our experimental results provide valuable insights into the comparative performance of these models in predicting stock prices, contributing to a deeper understanding of their applicability in Indian financial markets.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Analysis of CNN-Based Deep Learning Models: Evaluating the Impact of Transfer Learning on Model Accuracy
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: This paper conducts a comprehensive analysis of Convolutional Neural Network (CNN)-based deep learning models, focusing on the impact of transfer learning on their accuracy. Multiple tailored CNN architectures are implemented for image classification tasks, serving as baseline models with carefully selected architecture and hyperparameters. To boost performance, transfer learning is introduced using pre-trained CNN models (ResNet, EfficientNet) on large-scale image datasets. Transfer learning is applied at various stages, and its influence on convergence speed and final accuracy is investigated. The study meticulously records and compares results between CNN models with and without transfer learning, exploring metrics like convergence, training time, and final accuracy. This study investigates the role of transfer learning in improving the performance of CNN-based image classification. The results provide actionable insights for computer vision researchers and practitioners, helping to optimize deep learning techniques for image classification and similar tasks. By understanding how transfer learning influences CNN models, this research contributes to advancing efficiency and innovation in the field.

articleTitle: EcoParali: A Smart Stubble Management System
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: EcoParali is an innovative platform designed to address the severe problem of stubble burning in northern India, particularly in states like Punjab, Haryana, and Uttar Pradesh. After harvesting, farmers often burn stubble-crop residue left in fields-to clear land quickly for the next crop. This practice leads to harmful air pollution, soil degradation, and severe health risks. EcoParali offers a sustainable alternative by converting this agricultural waste into valuable products like bioenergy, animal feed, and compost. The platform serves as a digital marketplace, connecting farmers, buyers (companies) and businesses that can reform and reuse the stubble. Proposed application has two main modules, i.e. farmer and buyer. The farmer and buyer module have feature of registration, stubble submission, transaction management, and secure payment processing. EcoParali empowers farmers to earn additional income and reducing environmental harm. Buyers can also have utilized the stubble as a raw material of fuel, pulp& paper, biochar, biofuel, etc. EcoParali aims to create long-term, sustainable change in farming practices, fostering a circular economy where agricultural waste is turned into economic opportunities for farmers and businesses alike.

articleTitle: Unmasking the Reality: A Comprehensive Study of Deepfake Identification Techniques and Their Expanding Terrain
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: The swift progression of deepfake-generating technologies has elicited much apprehension about their potential misuse in digital media, necessitating the development of efficient detection methods. This research aims to improve the precision of deepfake detection by the application of spatial-temporal feature engineering methods. A comparative comparison of advanced preprocessing techniques is performed to enhance the extraction of spatial and temporal indicators essential for detecting deepfake abnormalities. The study investigates the amalgamation of sophisticated machine learning and deep learning models with designed characteristics to get enhanced detection efficacy. Experimental assessments are conducted on benchmark datasets to verify the effectiveness of the suggested methodologies. The findings highlight the importance of effective preprocessing strategies in enhancing model generalizability and dependability, hence supporting the overarching goal of preserving digital authenticity.

articleTitle: Comprehensive asset surveillance and prediction modeling using real time data analytics
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: The rapid evolution in the technology industry highlights the importance of developing a more advanced asset tracking system. The need for efficient and accurate asset management has become crucial and predominant across various industries. This paper displays the utilization of low-cost, and energy efficient technologies like Seeed Studio XIAO nRF52840 and Arduino Uno in designing and implementation of an asset tracking system. The design of the system primarily focuses on providing real time location of an asset, improving its tracking accuracy and operational efficiency. This study practically demonstrates the use of inexpensive microcontroller platforms along with BLE technology so as to develop an asset tracking system, the scalable solution that can be implemented across various industries such as logistics, healthcare, and manufacturing.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of CNN and Transformer Models for Image Recognition in Autonomous Driving
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: An autonomous driving system requires efficient image recognition to interpret the environment, detect obstacles, and make real-time decisions. This study compares Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Vision Transformers (ViTs) for image recognition tasks in autonomous driving. CNNs achieve higher accuracy (92.5% vs. 91.2%) and faster inference times (25ms vs. 35ms), making them more suitable for real-time applications. ViTs, however, perform better in challenging conditions, such as low lighting and occlusions, by capturing detailed information across entire images. The findings suggest that both architectures offer distinct advantages and could be combined to enhance the reliability and efficiency of autonomous driving systems.

articleTitle: “A Novel Regularized Deep Learning Approach for Tuberculosis Risk Prediction”
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: Effective treatment of tuberculosis (TB) requires prompt and precise risk assessment, since it continues to be a major worldwide health concern. Labor-intensive and subjective approaches are frequently used in traditional methods. The neural network model for Tuberculosis risk categorization which includes the following categories: No_Risk, Low_Risk, Moderate_Risk, and High_Risk is found in this paper. Regularization, Batch normalization and the use of Reversed Linear unit (ReLU) activation functions is adopted by the model to enhance learning process. After successfully conducting the sophisticated and optimal simulation the proposed model attains 91% classification accuracy using a variety of physiological and clinical parameters. This potentially presents future deep learning techniques to automatically rate people for possible tuberculosis occurrence thus delivering a strong tool to medical practitioners to offer distinctive intervention techniques. With deep learning, the model is capable of detecting a very complex pattern and correlation between data sets inputs and its output, thus enhancing its predictive precision as well as offering recommendations that may assist in the early detection of actual clinical situations.

articleTitle: Enhancing Sugarcane Disease Diagnosis: UNET Architecture for Red Rot Identification
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: Image segmentation is an important part of many computer vision problems and existing approaches such as pixel by pixel classification and manual annotation can be either in efficient or inaccurate. This research explored the way UNET architecture can circumvent these constraints to yield accurate segmentation. A diverse image dataset was applied to the UNET, and then its performance compared to conventional segmentation methods. Its capability to capture both the local and global characteristics contributes to the model’s improved performance, especially in complex settings. To detect red rot disease in sugarcane, these characteristics were used with an accuracy of 97%. UNET can be further improved by integrating it with other deep-learning techniques and its future research should focus on optimizing UNET for special use cases. This technology can also be used by farmers and agricultural experts to better pinpoint and tackle crop diseases, which could lead to better harvest yields and less financial baggage.

articleTitle: Classification Techniques in Data Mining: A Comprehensive Study
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: Data mining classification techniques become increasingly relevant because it is sensible to bring meaningful patterns out from very large data sets; however, cross-comparison and comparison in terms of different domains, in terms of several classifiers that exist, is discussed inadequately. A systematic review of the five prime classification algorithms has been made for a large set of varied datasets that range from healthcare and finance domains up to social media domains. Employed a newly developed multi-metric evaluation approach, which included accuracy, F1-score, computation performance, and model explainability. With the use of the 15 datasets to evaluate 50,000 instances, ensemble algorithms—namely Random Forest and XGBoost—were found to perform steadily better than isolated base learning classifiers, achieving a respective average of 94.2 percent in contrast to 87.6 percent for isolated techniques. In addition, DNN appeared to perform outstandingly on high-dimensional features but was computationally 3.5 times more complex compared to the tree-based technique. The study also found an enormous trade-off between model complexity and interpretability: the simpler models retained 85% of the performance while presenting better explainability. Such findings show empirical evidence for selecting optimum classification techniques on domain requirements and computational constraints, further adding towards decision-making in real-life data-mining applications.

articleTitle: Context-Aware Legal Summarization using Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: Legal judgments are often lengthy and complex, making it difficult for legal professionals to efficiently extract relevant information such as legal principles, precedents, and case outcomes. While existing automatic summarization techniques have proven useful for general domains, they struggle to address the specific requirements of legal texts. This paper presents a novel context-aware summarization model fine-tuned using reinforcement learning (RL), designed to optimize summaries based on legal-specific criteria. By leveraging a custom reward function, our model enhances the extraction of essential components of judgments, such as legal principles and precedents, while maintaining clarity and coherence. We train and evaluate our model on a dataset of Indian Supreme Court judgments, demonstrating significant improvements in summary quality over baseline models. Our experiments show that RL fine-tuning leads to better alignment with legal requirements, as evidenced by both automatic metrics (ROUGE, BLEU) and domain-specific evaluations. This work offers a step forward in the application of AI to legal text processing, with potential implications for improving the efficiency of legal research and judgment analysis.

articleTitle: Advanced Image Dehazing Techniques using Optimized Filters and Globally Guided Image Filtering
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: This paper presents sophisticated methods for picture dehazing, focusing on an optimized filtering approach called LIF paired with GGIF. The proposed Low-pass Infinite Impulse Response (LIF) technique provides a reliable method for enhancing the image by reducing noise while retaining significant features such as edges and intricate patterns. LIF, unlike traditional methods, employs adaptive techniques for enhancing both gray-scale and colour images. It achieves this by utilizing Gaussian-weighted proximity and intensity modifications, resulting in improved detail clarity and reduced noise. The incorporation of LIF (Local Intensity Filtering) with GGIF (Global Guided Image Filtering) resulted in significant enhancement in performance for the dehazing application, showcasing a noticeable increase in the perceptual fog density metric throughout the test images. The experimental results validate that the approach significantly enhances image quality by reducing fog density, with an average enhancement of 41.33%.

articleTitle: Improved Ensemble Learning-based VM Migration Prediction Technique
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: Virtual Machine computing resources significantly impact cloud storage performance and, in this regard, need to be well managed to reduce operational expenses. The scheme for predicting VM migration proposed in this paper is based on the ensemble learning technique with CPU usage as the primary performance parameter. We also assess the XGBoost, Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, and K-Nearest Neighbors algorithms and compare the Stacking, Voting, and Blending ensemble approaches. We use the real-world VM time-series performance data collected from the GWA-T-13 Materna dataset for empirical validation. These findings show that ensemble approaches achieve higher accuracy and generalization when compared with the individual model. However, this work is helpful in understanding strategies for moving virtual machines and getting some advice for resource management in cloud environments.

articleTitle: Evaluating Self-Supervised Learning Models for Multi-Label Pathology Detection: A Benchmark Against Supervised Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: The analysis and objective of the current work is to check the performance of SSL Models in multi-label classification on the available dataset of NIH Chest X-ray images which is a large-scale medical imaging dataset.
