The performance of SSL models, Dino_v_bl6, Dino with ResNet-50, and MoCo (Momentum Contrast) has been evaluated against the supervised model ResNet. These models are supposed to train to detect multiple pathologies using chest X-ray images. We also note that self-supervised embedding models outperform traditional supervised learning to a significant extent, achieving similar or higher performance on a number of quantitative metrics when compared to the softmax supervised ResNet model. This also draws attention to the possibilities of using SSL for biosignal-specific medical images. Furthermore, SSL approaches offer a promising solution in scenarios where there is an overabundance of annotated datasets available for training models such as deep neural networks. The effectiveness of SSL approaches in addressing the problem of data annotation is also emphasized by this study.

articleTitle: Genetic Algorithm Based Deterministic Workflow Scheduling with Load Balancing
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: A crucial problem in cloud computing is load balancing, which makes it challenging to guarantee that services operate as intended in accordance with quality of service (QoS), performance reviews, and service contracts that cloud service providers (CSPs) demand of businesses. The main goal is to distribute workloads among computer resources in order to improve performance. Load balancing is categorized as an "NP-hard" problem due to the ample solution space and the time needed to identify the optimal solution. While only a few approaches may provide an exact answer in polynomial time, prior research shows that metaheuristic-based tactics can find correct solutions in a fair amount of time. We use a framework that integrates Neural Network Task Classification (N2TC) and Genetic Algorithm Task Assignment (GATA) for load balancing. By taking load balancing and task completion time into account, this approach seeks to maximize load distribution and reduce process execution time. Extensive simulations of application operations were carried out to evaluate the effectiveness of the suggested load-balancing strategy. Results have shown that the proposed framework outperforms tournament selection genetic algorithm (TSGA), Heterogeneous Earliest Finish Time (HEFT), and Performance Effective Task Scheduling (PETS) heuristics in terms of load balancing up to 4.52% and makespan by 6.47%.

articleTitle: A Novel Technique to Remove Noise from SAR Images by Equalizing Neighborhood Surrounding Values and Pixel Smoothing
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: Automatic Target Recognition (ATR) plays a crucial role in military operations to locate actual targets and response immediately. Target recognition is easier in Standard Operating Conditions (SOC) while it becomes very complex in Extended Operating Conditions (EOC) due to environmental noise, large depression variations, partial occlusion and limited training samples. Deep Learning (DL) has a wide applications in Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) Imagery. Interpretation of SAR images to recognize actual targets is a major challenge. Researchers from across the world has given different deep learning models for ATR and it is found that most of DL algorithms performs poor in EOC’s. We have increased samples of the Moving and Stationary Target Acquisition and Recognition (MSTAR) dataset by adding partially occluded targets, different levels of noise and multiple objects in samples of the MSTAR. This paper presents an Object Localization & Deep Learning-based model for ATR. Our model contains a noise removal phase using spatial filtering and feature extraction and also, classification using enhanced VGG-19. The performance of the proposed model is satisfactory.

Author Keywords: Moving and Stationary Target Acquisition and Recognition (MSTAR)

articleTitle: Evaluating the Necessity of Cloud Computing in Modern Industrial Applications: A Comprehensive Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: This study thoroughly assesses the need for cloud computing across industries, examining the ways in which it improves scalability, flexibility, and affordability. Through the use of cloud computing, industries may update their IT infrastructure and move from outdated, capital-intensive models to more adaptable and effective cloud-based solutions. The report examines how cloud services like Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS), Platform as a Service (PaaS), and Software as a Service (SaaS) are integrated into key industries like manufacturing, healthcare, finance, and retail. Through the implementation of cutting-edge technologies like Internet of Things (IoT), machine learning (ML), and artificial intelligence (Al), cloud computing stimulates innovation, optimizes operations, and improves decision-making via data-driven insights. The growing significance of hybrid and multi-cloud strategies—which offer increased flexibility and enable industries to optimize resources and enhance performance—is also covered in the study. The study discusses the difficulties that sectors encounter in implementing cloud computing, along with its advantages. These difficulties include worries about data security, regulatory compliance, and cloud management. Strong security frameworks and efficient governance models are highlighted as essential elements of successful cloud integration. This study presents a framework for adopting cloud-based solutions for industries and emphasizes the significance of cloud computing as a fundamental technology for contemporary industrial applications.

articleTitle: Driver Distraction Detection System with Categorized Alerting based on SVM and PCA Optimization
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: The road accident scenario in India can be understood by simple statistics, and that every year more than 1.5 Lakh people lose their lives on the road. This is like crashing a jumbo jet carrying 340 people every day without any survivors. This is the enormity of the situation. Road accidents impact India’s GDP by 3.14% (IIT Delhi-TRIPP Study). This paper mainly focuses on the solution to the issue of distracted driving. Distracted driving is an act of indulging in attention-breaking activities while driving that can disrupt the flow of the driver’s coordination on the road. These distractions can be broadly classified as Manual, Visual, and Cognitive. The following research work shows how driver distractions can be detected using computer vision equipped cameras in vehicles to detect an act of distraction. We have used the State Farm Distracted Driver Detection Dataset (SFDDD), which consists of a set of images classified into 9 categories of driver distraction activities. We have adopted a Machine Learning approach and have trained a classification model using Linear Support Vector Machine (SVM), achieving an accuracy of 98.95%. The result has a trade-off with the time and space and was further improved by merging SVM with Principal Component Analysis (PCA) that significantly reduced the model training time and even enhanced the accuracy to 99%. Using the model, we have also implemented a prototype for prioritized alerting system that warns the driver as soon as it detects a distraction and sets off an alarm.

articleTitle: High Degree Dependency Study of Ensemble Models in Credit Card Fraud Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: Credit card fraud detection is an increasingly critical issue due to the growth of digital transactions and the sophistication of fraudulent activities. This study proposes a hybrid framework combining Graph Neural Networks (GNNs), ensemble methods (e.g., XGBoost, Random Forest), and polynomial feature engineering to address key challenges, including class imbalance, non-linear data relationships, and real-time applicability. The system achieved a detection accuracy of 96.7%, precision of 96.9%, recall of 96.4%, and a false-negative rate of 3.6% on benchmark datasets. These improvements are attributed to the integration of advanced sampling techniques, polynomial feature transformations, and the hybrid architecture. The findings demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in enhancing fraud detection systems and provide a scalable solution for real-world applications.

articleTitle: UniManage – An All-in-One Platform for Empowering Businesses
publicationTitle: 2025 2nd International Conference on Computational Intelligence, Communication Technology and Networking (CICTN)
abstract: UniManage is basically all packaged into one, fully-fledged SaaS solution that has been designed to bring together major business functions into one excellent system that optimizes organizational processes. Its modules are flexible and span meetings, collaboration, accounting, finance, and supply chain management. With this, it can attend to many business needs. By being modular, UniManage will allow organizations to create solutions that fit the requirements of their operations and workflows specifically. This has been a major advantage for UniManage. Software laundry will significantly decline, workflows will be optimized and increased overall productivity across organizations will be achieved. Flexibility, robust features, and user-centric design make UniManage certainly an essential tool for businesses intent on streamlining operations. It increases efficiency while also allowing teams to work better, so they stay in sync and can meet their goals. This is how well UniManage is positioned as a solution that is flexible or scalable according to the demands of today's business scenarios: a reliable foundation for growth and innovation.
